Friend,

Stand In The Gap Foundation was born out of January 6. For years, we stood beside those families. We paid for lawyers, covered rent, sat in courtrooms, and made sure nobody went through it alone.

What we learned in those years is why I'm writing to you today.

**The lawfare that came down on January 6 families wasn't built for them, and it didn't stop with them.**

So we widened the fight. Everything we built for those families now lives inside our Stand for Justice initiative, and Stand for Justice is now open to anyone the federal system has run over.

January 6 families aren't going anywhere. They're still with us. They're just no longer the only ones we can help.

Yesterday, I mailed the letter that opens this new chapter.

It went to the Office of the Pardon Attorney at the U.S. Department of Justice. It's about a man named Dr. Michael Rimlawi. His patients call him Dr. Mike.

Dr. Mike is a spine surgeon from Dallas. For twenty years, people came to him when they couldn't sit through a workday, couldn't pick up their kids, couldn't sleep through the night. He did the small-incision kind of spine surgery. Less cutting, less blood, and most patients home the same day or the next.

Then the federal government went after the hospital where he operated.

Forest Park Medical Center paid a marketing firm to advertise its surgeons, something hospitals all over this country do every day. Prosecutors called it a kickback. Dr. Mike wasn't charged with hurting a patient. He wasn't charged with billing for a surgery that never happened.

A jury convicted him in 2019. In 2021, a federal judge sentenced him to 90 months in prison, seven and a half years, and ordered him to pay $28,839,201.68 in restitution.

To insurance companies.

The Supreme Court refused to hear his case. Justice Gorsuch wrote that he would have heard it, because a judge, not a jury, set that $28.8 million.

Dr. Mike did his time. He's home now with his wife and their two young sons. But unless something changes, that debt follows him for twenty years after his release. And a pardon alone won't erase it. The pardon has to say so.

So our letter asks for two things: a full pardon, and that the pardon wipe out every dollar of restitution he hasn't paid.

Friend, Dr. Mike was nowhere near the Capitol. But if you've followed what happened to January 6 families, you already know this story. A prosecution built to make an example. A sentence that ends on paper and keeps going in real life. Restitution that follows a man home and sits at his kitchen table.

Different courtroom. Same pattern.

That's why Dr. Mike is the first story we're telling from the new Stand for Justice. He won't be the last.

subject: Reminder: 🚨 Your Weekly Update From The NEGOP
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Nebraska Republican Party 1610 N St
body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| Letter from the Chair...
---
| Thank you to everyone who mailed, texted, or shared slate cards; who found locations and delivered signs; and who door-knocked, phone-called, and wrote personal notes. Thank you as well to our poll watchers and observers. Nebraska's Republican candidates would not have succeeded without you.
Your work paid off in important ways. Nationally, Nebraska is recognized as a state that pushed back the Democrats' blue wave. We are viewed as a bright spot. A special thank-you is owed once again to the Third Congressional District. As I said at the Vice President JD Vance rally, the First and Second Districts are our front lines, but we rely on the Third District as our rear guard--to stop any of the nonsense that gets past the eastern part of the state. The Third District did not disappoint. Voter loyalty to the Party and good Nebraska common sense prevailed.
We re-elected all of our congressional incumbents. Congressman Mike Flood's race was closer than any of us watching were comfortable with, and the rural counties of the First District made the difference. Thank you. Many of our neighboring states, and the country as a whole, fared far worse.
Second District congressional candidate Brinker Harding was unsuccessful. Given the environment, I don't know of anyone who could have won with an "R" beside their name. Brinker and his team ran a strong campaign, but it was not enough. All of our constitutional state officers won re-election, and our new nominee for Secretary of State, Scott Petersen, won handily. The margins were not as strong as we normally see for statewide offices, but again the Third District carried us through. The brightest spot in our state elections was the State Board of Education. We now hold a 5-3 majority. Congratulations to Elizabeth Tegtmeier, Angie Eberspacher, Sherry Jones, and Lou Ann Goding for stepping up to run or re-run and enduring the attacks from the left. A special thank-you goes to SBOE member Kirk Penner for his help in these races. Lou Ann Goding is one of the few Republicans who narrowly won in Douglas County; she will be an excellent addition to the board. Like SBOE member Lisa Schonhoff, she is data-driven and no-nonsense.
Our University of Nebraska Board of Regents races were won by liberal candidates. We had an outstanding candidate in Dr. Jeremy Hosein, but he was outspent, and the urban areas of Lancaster County preferred the "Independent" Democrat consultant Brent Comstock.
We appear to have lost three seats in the Unicameral, though some races remain very close and provisional ballots are still being counted. Overall it could have been much worse. We elected and re-elected some very strong conservatives, and I am grateful to each of them. Taylor Royal and Senator Brad von Gillern narrowly lost races they would have served well in. Rebecca Rens, Chris Anderson, and Tobias Howard put up valiant efforts in what proved to be a nearly impossible year for new candidates in urban areas, no matter how hard they worked.
Douglas and Lancaster County Republicans did not fare well. Both counties lost their races for County Attorney and Sheriff. Our eastern urban districts will now bear the consequences of those decisions--growing homeless encampments, lower arrest rates, lighter sentencing requests, and little to no cooperation with Immigration and Customs Enforcement. I hope that I am wrong, but fear that I am not. Once again, thank you. Each of you knows the work you put into this election. I am humbled to serve alongside you.
I promise to wake up every day continuing to safeguard our values and to prepare us for the 2028 election. There is no surrender. Our values - love of God, family, state and nation - are too precious to do any less. God is good. He will see us through this time and be the protection we need over our state and our nation.
God bless Nebraska and God bless America.
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair... | Thank you to everyone who mailed, texted, or shared slate cards; who found locations and delivered signs; and who door-knocked, phone-called, and wrote personal notes. Thank you as well to our poll watchers and observers. Nebraska's Republican candidates would not have succeeded without you. Your work paid off in important ways. Nationally, Nebraska is recognized as a state that pushed back the Democrats' blue wave. We are viewed as a bright spot. A special thank-you is owed once again to the Third Congressional District. As I said at the Vice President JD Vance rally, the First and Second Districts are our front lines, but we rely on the Third District as our rear guard--to stop any of the nonsense that gets past the eastern part of the state. The Third District did not disappoint. Voter loyalty to the Party and good Nebraska common sense prevailed. We re-elected all of our congressional incumbents. Congressman Mike Flood's race was closer than any of us watching were comfortable with, and the rural counties of the First District made the difference. Thank you. Many of our neighboring states, and the country as a whole, fared far worse. Second District congressional candidate Brinker Harding was unsuccessful. Given the environment, I don't know of anyone who could have won with an "R" beside their name. Brinker and his team ran a strong campaign, but it was not enough. All of our constitutional state officers won re-election, and our new nominee for Secretary of State, Scott Petersen, won handily. The margins were not as strong as we normally see for statewide offices, but again the Third District carried us through. The brightest spot in our state elections was the State Board of Education. We now hold a 5-3 majority. Congratulations to Elizabeth Tegtmeier, Angie Eberspacher, Sherry Jones, and Lou Ann Goding for stepping up to run or re-run and enduring the attacks from the left. A special thank-you goes to SBOE member Kirk Penner for his help in these races. Lou Ann Goding is one of the few Republicans who narrowly won in Douglas County; she will be an excellent addition to the board. Like SBOE member Lisa Schonhoff, she is data-driven and no-nonsense. Our University of Nebraska Board of Regents races were won by liberal candidates. We had an outstanding candidate in Dr. Jeremy Hosein, but he was outspent, and the urban areas of Lancaster County preferred the "Independent" Democrat consultant Brent Comstock. We appear to have lost three seats in the Unicameral, though some races remain very close and provisional ballots are still being counted. Overall it could have been much worse. We elected and re-elected some very strong conservatives, and I am grateful to each of them. Taylor Royal and Senator Brad von Gillern narrowly lost races they would have served well in. Rebecca Rens, Chris Anderson, and Tobias Howard put up valiant efforts in what proved to be a nearly impossible year for new candidates in urban areas, no matter how hard they worked. Douglas and Lancaster County Republicans did not fare well. Both counties lost their races for County Attorney and Sheriff. Our eastern urban districts will now bear the consequences of those decisions--growing homeless encampments, lower arrest rates, lighter sentencing requests, and little to no cooperation with Immigration and Customs Enforcement. I hope that I am wrong, but fear that I am not. Once again, thank you. Each of you knows the work you put into this election. I am humbled to serve alongside you. I promise to wake up every day continuing to safeguard our values and to prepare us for the 2028 election. There is no surrender. Our values - love of God, family, state and nation - are too precious to do any less. God is good. He will see us through this time and be the protection we need over our state and our nation. God bless Nebraska and God bless America. name: Douglas Carswell
subject: Under the Floodlights
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://us18.campaign-archive.com/?e=5703353baa&u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=77a2b64374)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
I watched my first game of football five years ago. I’m now utterly addicted. As a Brit, I grew up watching cricket and soccer. I played rugby and fenced for my university. So hear it from me: there is no sporting contest as exhilarating as your version of football. A football game can turn on a dime. An interception, or the diving catch by a wide receiver, and the entire game can switch in seconds. At the FIFA World Cup this summer, a close soccer game meant one side winning 2-1, with long periods in which the ball was simply passed around. In American football, games are often decided in the final few seconds. When Ole Miss lost to Texas the other week, it came down to the final throw into the end zone — and in my view, the wrong side caught it. The longer I watch football, the more I have come to appreciate the game’s depth. At first my eyes always followed the ball — from snap to quarterback, then looking to see what he might do with it. Now I realize football is a performance with so many different subplots. You need to keep an eye on the wide receivers and the running backs. There is an endless series of moves and counter moves. No other sport I know is as multilayered. I might be new to your sport, but I have a clear idea of what I like to watch. College football over the NFL. High school football above everything. Friday night lights is not just a game of football. It’s an event. Almost two hundred years ago, Frenchman Alexis de Tocqueville toured America and marveled at the richness of your civic society. You don’t need to have read him to see what he was on about. I see what he meant every Friday night during football season. Not every kid is cut out to be a quarterback or wide receiver. Not everyone is suited to cheer. But at the local high school football game, there is a role for everyone — in the band or the pep squad, filming the game or directing the drone. Or simply cheering on their side. I spent nine years enjoying the finest of the British education system. Not once can I recall more than a fraction of the school turning out to cheer on a school team. On one of the rare occasions I missed a Friday night football game in the past few years, it was because I was on a delayed flight back from Atlanta. Annoyed to be missing the game, I found solace in peering out the window at the floodlights of scores of high school stadiums far below. I realized for the first time that what happens at your local high school happens across America. No other sport I know teaches players, and those watching, about more than just the game. This season I have especially enjoyed watching Jackson Prep play. Ahead of the playoffs, they have lost only once. Oddly, perhaps, it was watching them the one time they lost that makes me most proud of them. Down 28-10, the game had seemed settled. A lesser team would have limped along, accepting their fate. Not this team. Instead, they clawed their way back — 15 points in a few minutes. The opponents commanding lead evaporated. Never have I seen a team play with such grit and determination. Sure, they still lost narrowly. All teams lose sometimes. But a team that can rally like that has learned something beyond football — something that will serve them well long after that game is a distant memory. Football coaches that teach a team to play like that are doing something right, no matter the score. A school that produces students with the character to play like that has got the most important lessons that can be taught right. A society that can produce young men with that attitude is going to be okay, no matter what the future throws at it. To be born American is to have won first prize in the lottery of life. To be an American watching Friday night football is to be cashing in the prize. A great team is not defined by the score of any one game, just as a good student is not defined by one set of test grades. Nor should a great country – and I make the point this week for a reason – be defined by any one set of election results. Scores, grades, even election results: in the end, all of them derive from character and culture. Rejoice in football. Glory in the many American virtues that come alive under those floodlights. Do that, and all will be well. I love football.

name: Doug Truax
subject: The count that doesn't add up
body:
Every election's numbers should add up, and most states could make sure they do.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e5583628/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvNllSd1Y1ZHFTQg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDc/LbmNsejFCdGxMNA/qP2hpZHM9bmNSdlBTRzBQSE1EbHhscw/gau8z6Q/s8v31f1e33e)
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | | Patriot,
---
Here's a question that ought to have a simple answer: ** _how many ballots were cast in your state in November 2024?_** Our research team at the **Voter Reference Foundation** set out to answer it three ways, using nothing but official government sources. **_First_** , the total ballots cast that the state itself certified. **_Second_** , the number of registered voters the state's own records show as having voted. **_Third_** , the figure the state reported to the federal Election Assistance Commission. In a system running the way it should, those three numbers match, or come close with a clear, documented explanation for any gap. **In nearly every state we looked at, they didn't match.******In some places _all three disagreed with each other at the same time_ , meaning no two official sources could agree on how many ballots were cast in the same election. I spent years running a business before I got into this work. If my company kept three sets of records that disagreed on how many customers we'd served, somebody would be explaining it to me before lunch. The biggest of these problems surprised even me. **Most states never save a certified copy of the voter roll as it stood on Election Day.** The voter list a living database. People move, pass away, and register every single day, and the file keeps getting edited in place. By the time anyone outside government can get a copy, it's a different list from the one that existed when the polls closed. The starting point you'd need to check the count is simply gone. _Why should that bother you?_ Because a gap nobody can explain never stays quiet for long. **When trust in our elections is already stretched thin** , an unexplained number gets filled in with whatever story people are inclined to believe. Accurate, checkable numbers are what make honest results hard to attack. **Here’s the encouraging part.** The fix is simple, and it doesn’t take a new law. _Election offices just need to save a copy of the voter list the night the polls close and report one plain number for how many people voted. Then anyone could line the two up and see whether they match._ Most election offices already have this information. They just don’t make it public. On November 3rd, Americans in every state will cast ballots in the 2026 midterms. Unless something changes, most of those states will once again edit their rolls in place and move on, and the chance to check that election's count will slip away with it. **We want to be in position to press election offices to adopt these fixes, and to run this same comparison on the 2026 results as soon as the data is available.** _I'd like to ask you to do two things before then..._ The first costs nothing. Contact your county election office and ask them a single question: "Will you keep a certified copy of the voter roll as it stands when the polls close on Election Day?" It's a fair, polite question, and it's exactly the kind a local official ought to hear from the voters they serve. _**[The second is to stand with us today with a gift of $35, or whatever you can manage. Your support keeps the records on Voteref.com current, so there's something reliable to check the count against. It funds the research behind reports like this one. And it lets us keep pressing election offices on these fixes before and after November.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**_
---
[ **CHIP IN $35 BEFORE NOVEMBER 3****RD** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
When those three sets of numbers finally agree, nobody will have to take anyone's word for the result, including mine. Trust, but verify.
---
| | | Let freedom ring,
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Doug Truax Founder & CEO Voter Reference Foundation
---
P.S. **[If you're in a position to do more, a gift of $1,000 can cover acquiring and publishing an entire state's voter file in some states.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** And if you'd like to see the evidence before you give anything, the full report is on our website, methodology and all. Read it, then decide.

By now you've probably understood that I write about what the mainstream media ignores. Well, in August of 2026, a small army of federal deputies did something no agency in Ohio history had ever done: they found _seventy-nine_ missing children in a single month. The operation was called Meridian. It ran from August 1st through August 31st across the Northern and Southern Districts of Ohio, and when the U.S. Marshals Service announced its conclusion on September 8th, they described it accurately -- _the largest missing-child operation in the state 's history_.
Seventy-nine children. Ages six to seventeen. Six years old.
Consider what the Marshals actually are. Their charter is manhunting -- violent fugitives, escapees, the worst of the worst. In Operation Meridian, they turned that machinery around and pointed it at the smallest and most vulnerable people in America. Deputy U.S. Marshals Pete Elliott of the Northern District and Michael Black of the Southern District applied the same intelligence, surveillance, and task-force methods they use to corner killers, and used them to knock on doors, chase down tips, and pull kids out of danger. As Black put it, they used the resources and methods of their fugitive task forces to find children instead...

The operation was called Meridian. It ran from August 1st through August 31st across the Northern and Southern Districts of Ohio, and when the U.S. Marshals Service announced its conclusion on September 8th, they described it accurately -- the largest missing-child operation in the state 's history. **The Arrest**
On Thursday night, October 22, agents from the FBI and the DEA walked into a residential neighborhood on the north side of Eagle Pass, Texas, and escorted out one of the border's binational businessmen. Mexican papers name him Julio Rodolfo Gonzalez Olveda -- a fuel-and-trucking operator with his life and his companies on both sides of the Rio Grande. Vanguardia calls him "mexicoamericano"; Zocalo calls him "nigropetense", a son of Piedras Negras, the factory city across the river. As of Sunday, October 25, not one English-language outlet appears to have reported the arrest. The coverage is entirely Spanish and almost entirely local: Vanguardia, Reforma, Zocalo, Factor Coahuila.
**The Charge**
What the Mexican reports say, carefully: Gonzalez faces a federal charge of conspiracy to commit money laundering, tied to the alleged illegal transport of fuel from Texas into Mexico. Vanguardia and Factor Coahuila both credit the FBI and DEA. Vanguardia describes a months-long binational investigation between U.S. and Mexican authorities, and reports that the U.S. case may be sealed. Every verb in the Mexican copy is *presunto* -- alleged. No U.S. docket is visible, and Gonzalez hasn't spoken publicly. But a sealed indictment in a multi-defendant fuel case usually buys one thing: time. More knock-on-the-door mornings may be on the calendar.
**The Racket...**

Peggy Flanagan is the first Native American woman ever elected to the United States Senate. A 237-year wait is finally over. Deb Haaland is the first Native American woman ever elected governor of any state — in New Mexico, which barred her people from voting until 1948. Sharice Davids held Kansas. Claire Valdez won New York with 83%. Four of our five Indigenous women were elected, in a historic night for Democrats powered by people like you. And then there's Alaska. body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=20%2E6803%2EQgPBxz)
Hi
What a week! We made the impossible possible on Election Night. The whole country is taking notice, so wanted to share a few headlines that show just how much we've accomplished together:
**Democrat Will Lawrence Wins In Michigan, Proving Potency Of Anti-Data Center Politics** – Huffington Post
---
Where there’s a Will, there’s a way! Will Lawrence never shied away from his values on the campaign trail. From Day 1, he called for a national moratorium on new data centers to give his community a say in these projects before they’re forced into their neighborhoods. **Will is proving that climate is, in fact, a winning issue, and clearly the nation is taking note!**
**Democrats’ Big Statehouse Wins Could Transform Climate and Energy Policy** – Inside Climate News
---
We’ve always said real climate power starts in our statehouses. That’s why the JanePAC Team backed leaders from Michigan to Pennsylvania to Arizona to North Carolina who were actually willing to go toe-to-toe with the fossil fuel industry. **We’ve secured a Democratic trifecta in 5/6 of the states we invested in, turning unthinkable victories into real governing power for climate champions.**
**Texas data centers face uncertain future after Hinojosa wins governor’s race** — Reuters
---
We’re not surprised AI developers are quaking in their boots. **After years of Greg Abbott rolling out the red carpet for Big Tech, Gina Hinojosa is turning Texas politics on its head.** She's ready to halt new data center approvals and end the sweetheart tax breaks these corporations have enjoyed for far too long.
* * *
There were moments this cycle when the odds felt stacked against us. But every single time we had a moment of doubt, our movement proved that people power is the antidote to despair. We organized, we mobilized, and we won.
We couldn’t do this without you.
Every neighbor you talked to. Every single action you took. **That collective grit is what brought us this victory.**
But we can’t afford to let up now. Big Oil and their billionaire backers aren’t giving up. They’re getting ready now to pour corporate cash into the next cycle to stop our progress and silence our voices.
**Now, we have to defend our ground and elect even more leaders with the moral courage to put people over corporate profits.**
**[Will you make a contribution of any amount you can so we can keep this momentum going and protect our wins?](https://act.janepac.com/go/9?c0=ms_jfcp_em_20261107-ak.OPQrMb&amount=5&refcode=em20261107-20&t=3&akid=20%2E6803%2EQgPBxz)**

In solidarity,
Team JanePAC

body:
Our lives are not temporary or disposable. Home is here. | | | Peter, It’s Saturday, and immigrant workers are doing what they do every day: covering shifts in our hospitals, taking their kids to practice, and running small businesses. They want what every working person wants: to live, work, and raise their families with safety, stability, and security. Instead, they’re being treated as disposable while our communities live through the largest mass delegalization effort in modern U.S. history. **[Chip in $10 today to power the organizing that protects our communities and fights for economic stability for all.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqswjENXoYacFGtlMLXh6NAeabdGGvthn4g7RETlfNxxCD_F99e1on29UFO2iG0BJy0EiMXZStjYteLKNA85gqD33uwAmcLhpgRD-XCZPmRbeCJitdvVa-HnISPKC_MxhnqqHzPcY_vitKO82rKQxTS03UH6qHGl1OA1sipOVLd5c2Do6Ub2O8x_8R434wWQf7JIhaZmGQo00C37_DvK9ogElhhDF9zEIGsFTID7lhDlpZ9Nhb5FyF-i7wyQRS5_9pQBtlRqykyC8flO-zvnyBMaYRhRAYiZtGHlyWYG0PPqGO9oALwOGz7cwsz4nO7DjA_T8sln2Fj7gGmOQmWt48k8TsiLXh8DphaA8XAYlstv52X5BOJY5fVuQ8-u-_qJGG6TJDcX7ayOv5CdT6cuL1GBkxVlv5nX0KNHk2to2jOAAed5a0OH74D-ILfDv6cseFOqP07nl0mEqQApX9q58HQp/4vj/QNNcU-rRRCOm6bEKsgkd_Q/h0/h001.pxmzjfzpRlM-3Shqrf7MWnbTpZlDqzXgmak11PXEpfQ)** A functioning economy relies on stability. When working people lose status, communities lose teachers, healthcare workers, caregivers, entrepreneurs, and taxpayers. Right now, more than a million TPS holders are losing the protections and work permits they’ve held for years, if not decades. DACA is being chipped away piece by piece, from court decisions to USCIS renewal delays, stripping tens of thousands of recipients of their jobs, income, and status. clean_body: Our lives are not temporary or disposable. Home is here. | | | Peter, It’s Saturday, and immigrant workers are doing what they do every day: covering shifts in our hospitals, taking their kids to practice, and running small businesses. They want what every working person wants: to live, work, and raise their families with safety, stability, and security. Instead, they’re being treated as disposable while our communities live through the largest mass delegalization effort in modern U.S. history. A functioning economy relies on stability. When working people lose status, communities lose teachers, healthcare workers, caregivers, entrepreneurs, and taxpayers. Right now, more than a million TPS holders are losing the protections and work permits they’ve held for years, if not decades. DACA is being chipped away piece by piece, from court decisions to USCIS renewal delays, stripping tens of thousands of recipients of their jobs, income, and status. And billions of our hard-earned tax dollars are funding agencies whose mass raids, detentions, and deportations are tearing families and neighbors apart and making an already difficult economy even harder. You cannot put working people first while leaving immigrant workers behind. Economic justice and immigrant justice are inseparable. Temporary protections are not a substitute for permanent status. Citizenship is the only solution to the chaos and instability that mass delegalization is creating, and Congress must deliver it. clean_body: Peter, We face powerful foes today who are willing to do anything to dominate America, even if it means destroying democracy. The Left's so-called principles are utterly incompatible with those that are the bedrock of our constitutional republic. They're incompatible with individual liberty and free will. They're incompatible with the Judeo-Christian belief system under which this nation was founded. At a time when the very values that make America great are under attack, we must continue to stand strong. We must make sure our fellow citizens understand the seriousness of this situation. I'll never stop defending America, our Constitution, our free market economy, and our Judeo-Christian traditions. And I'll never stop calling out the leftiFIGHTLS who want to tear our country down. I know you won't either! I do a lot of things. But one of the most important things I do is work with my colleagues at Landmark Legal Foundation. Landmark Legal Foundation is on a mission. They 're here to protect liberty, property rights, constitutionalism . . . in other words, what you read in the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution. And now, I'd love you to stand with me in supporting this outstanding organization. The Left aren't saviors of democracy.They 're MarxiFIGHTLS. And what they're doing is destroying the country. They fight desperately to undermine our election processes and, if elections go against them, they use the courts to obstruct the policies We the People voted for. They persecute their opponents, like when the Biden In justice Department waged relentless lawfare against Trump and his allies. LeftiFIGHTLS focus so much energy on the justice system - to control it, to contort it, to use it to promote their insanely radical agenda. Again and again, they turn to rogue left-wing judges to usurp the Constitution and undermine America's founding principles. We must not be silent while these leftiFIGHTLS destroy our republic from within. That 's why it's so great to have Landmark Legal Foundation take them on! I love these guys. I've been part of the Landmark family for over three decades . . . as president for 20 years, then Chairman of the Board, and now Chairman Emeritus. These briefs present the strongest possible argument for the constitutional position and help convince judges to do the right thing. In 2024, Landmark made a historic winning argument that special prosecutor Jack Smith lacked the legal authority to target Donald Trump in the classified documents probe. The judge in the case echoed Landmark's arguments in her decision and delivered a huge win over the Left 's lawfare. Landmark also fights to defend free, fair elections. For example, Landmark filed a supportive brief in another key election integrity case. With Bost v. Illinois Board of Elections , they're helping challenge unfair vote-by-mail procedures. Here, Illinois Congressman Mike Bost sued the Illinois Board of Elections over their practice of counting mail-in ballots received after Election Day. Such counting delays results and opens the door for abuse. When the Supreme Court agreed, it marked a major victory for free, fair elections. But this is not the last fight! This isn't political . . . it 's about the Constitution! My Landmark friends are on the frontlines of the battle to preserve our country. They're a vital part of the conservative, constitutionalist force fighting for our country today. Your support will help Landmark Legal Foundation live up to its motto of " Defending Liberty, Fighting Tyranny." Thank you in advance for actively joining the fight! An Israeli soldier places his hand on the shoulder of an armed Israeli settler in the Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta neighborhood of Jericho, in the occupied West Bank, on November 5, 2026, a day after settlers violently seized Palestinian homes in the neighborhood. Photo by Katrine Dige Houmøller for Drop Site News.
JERICHO, Occupied West Bank--"They beat all of us. Children, women, and men," Mustafa Kaaba said, standing on a dusty street in the city of Jericho in the occupied West Bank. The night before, November 4, armed Israeli settlers burst into his home and the homes of his neighbors, ransacking them, violently forcing the families out, and warning them not to return.
Kaaba clutched his head and struggled to lift his arm, which was visibly swollen and bruised after settlers beat him with sticks. Around him, his family's belongings lay scattered across the street. Kaaba's pregnant wife, Fatima, gathered what was left of their clothes and stuffed them into plastic bags. After being expelled from their home, the family of seven was forced to sleep in their car and on the street.
"They ripped up the children's schoolbooks and books written in Arabic," Fatima told Drop Site. "They didn't even leave our children anything to study with." Fatima said the settlers took their refrigerator, washing machine, television, and entire bedroom set to another apartment seized by the settlers.
Around her, children ran between piles of rubble and scattered sheep that wandered out from a nearby corrugated metal shed. The couple's young daughter had been in a playful mood, running up to people for hugs. Then, without warning, she burst into tears, screaming and running away from those around her. Her father tried in vain to comfort her. "She is having a panic attack," Kaaba said. "I think it's triggered by the trauma from last night."
The family is now afraid to walk around Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta, their neighborhood on the outskirts of the city. "It's dangerous, even just getting to the end of this street. I swear, it's dangerous. What if they come after us?" Kaaba said. "We don't have anything left."
Fatima stood nearby clutching a piece of clothing. "Our house is still standing, but they told us not to come back," she added. "They say it belongs to them now."
LEFT: Mustafa Kaaba and Fatima Kaaba's children look through the belongings of their home in Jericho after Israeli settlers stormed the family's home the previous night and forced them out. RIGHT: Mustafa and Fatima Kaaba's youngest child looks through her empty schoolbag shortly before suffering a panic attack, which her father attributed to the previous night's raid, in Jericho, occupied West Bank. November 5, 2026. Photos by Katrine Dige Houmøller for Drop Site News.
According to residents, at least 13 Palestinian households were driven from their homes in Jericho by some 30 Israeli settlers, some of them masked, who rampaged through the neighborhood.
The next morning, the settlers made their occupation known. They hung Israeli flags from the balconies and entrances of multiple houses--a standard marker of a Palestinian home taken over by settlers. Armed men patrolled between the newly occupied homes--with rifles slung over their shoulders or pistols tucked into their waistbands. Israeli women and children wandered along the gravel roads. Young men sat outside reading the Torah while gunmen stood guard at every property.
The expansion of Israeli settlements and outposts across the occupied West Bank over the past three years has been rapid and increasingly violent. More than 6,400 Palestinians, including over 3,100 children, were displaced between January 2023 and August 2026 as a result of settler attacks and restrictions on access to their land, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/0c58b139-20ff-4409-a940-36e736e7d053?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. At least 48 Palestinian communities were completely emptied of their residents during that period.
Even in that context, the takeover by Israeli settlers of homes inside a Palestinian city in the occupied West Bank represents a dangerous escalation in Israel's dispossession of Palestinians across the territory. Some Palestinians are comparing it to the situation in Hebron, the largest city in the West Bank and the only one to have Israeli settlements inside the heart of the city.
Most Israeli settlements surround Palestinian towns and cities, usually on the surrounding hilltops, but in Hebron armed Israeli settlers live in the midst of Palestinian residents and are guarded by a permanent and large deployment of Israeli troops, making Hebron one of the most [tightly controlled](https://substack.com/redirect/1a9dc3c3-a4ff-4d9d-8bd1-cb05a906b5fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and ethnically segregated urban areas in the West Bank with Palestinians even prevented from walking down certain streets.
"Establishing a settlement inside Jericho poses a security threat and constitutes a geopolitical disaster that must not be allowed to happen. This move is designed to deepen friction and violence, entrench an apartheid regime, and foreclose any possibility of a future political agreement," the Israeli group Peace Now, that organizes against settlements in the West Bank, warned in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/94c7d9ee-3569-4e1f-b92c-18fe96fc85f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The violent home seizures on Wednesday came after a gradual buildup. The neighborhood of Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta had been experiencing repeated attacks by settlers, often from a nearby outpost called Palace Farms, according to Peace Now. Settlers also demolished around 13 homes in the area in February and again in July. Rubble is still scattered throughout the neighborhood.
By October 27, the day of the Israeli elections, settlers had already begun fencing off parts of the neighborhood and installing infrastructure, according to Peace Now, which also reported a number of break-ins, thefts, and assaults on residents. A gate was erected to block access to an entire street, cutting off dozens of Palestinian homes. Now, the settlers have taken over some of those homes.
The Israeli military did nothing to stop the violent takeover, with multiple Palestinian residents telling Drop Site that troops stood by as families were forced out.
The following morning, Israeli military vehicles repeatedly drove through the neighborhood. Uniformed soldiers warmly greeted the settlers, shook hands, and embraced them. Some entered the occupied houses, appearing familiar with the settlers inside.
Outside one of the newly occupied properties, a settler sat in a chair keeping guard. "They're good friends of the families now," he said as soldiers walked into the house. "Since last night," he added.
LEFT: Israeli settlers move into Palestinian homes in Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta neighborhood of Jericho, in the occupied West Bank, on November 5, 2026. RIGHT: Israeli soldiers visit Israeli settler families throughout the day in Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta neighborhood of Jericho, in the occupied West Bank, after the settlers occupied several homes in the Palestinian city the previous night. Photos by Katrine Dige Houmøller for Drop Site News.
The properties are located on the outskirts of Jericho and technically in Area C--a designation under the Oslo Accords of the 1990s where Israel retains full civil and military control--right on the border of Area A, where the Palestinian Authority has nominal security and civil control, and where most of Jericho city is located.
The takeover was reportedly coordinated by the settlement organization Nachala and the Binyamin Regional Council. Both organizations claim that the properties were legally purchased. Jericho Governor Hussein Hamayel disputed the claims, saying in an interview with Raya Media Network that the land belongs to Jordan's state treasury and describing the alleged sales as forged.
In response to an inquiry from Drop Site, about the Israeli military's role in the takeover, accounts of violence and looting by settlers, and the settlers' continued occupation of the Palestinian homes, a military official said in a written response that "Upon the entry of Israeli civilians into homes in the area adjacent to Jericho, situational assessments and field patrols were conducted to examine the incident. In the coming week, the examination of the settlers' claims regarding the purchase of the lands will continue." The official also said "the action was carried out without prior coordination or approval from the IDF." They added, "The mission of the soldiers stationed at the military outpost in the area is to safeguard the security of all residents in the area and to prevent terror and additional confrontations."
Yet following the Israeli settlers' takeover of the homes, the Jericho neighborhood is increasingly off limits to Palestinians or perceived supporters. The morning after the attacks, settlers in an ATV recklessly chased Palestinian journalists through the streets, relentlessly pursuing them until they managed to escape the area.
Mahmoud Faridat, a resident of Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta, owns two farms directly adjacent to the newly occupied properties. The following morning, Faridat went to herd his sheep inside one of the farms with his brother, Jamal, and his nephew. They were stopped by settlers, who beat Jamal and the nephew and sprayed them with tear gas, Faridat said. Settlers had also erected another makeshift barrier, arranging chairs and wooden planks across the road to block access to Faridat's farmland.
"[A settler] told us not to go through it, but our water ponds and farm are all in front of the house," Faridat told Drop Site immediately after failing to reach his land.
"From the moment they [the settlers] came, they have attacked us." Even the main roads in the neighborhood have become dangerous.
"The street we're standing on now is still accessible, even though the army stops us to ask questions," Faridat said. "But tomorrow, Allah knows, they may not let us pass at all."

Please consider becoming a paid subscriber or making a . | | ---|---|--- An Israeli soldier places his hand on the shoulder of an armed Israeli settler in the Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta neighborhood of Jericho, in the occupied West Bank, on November 5, 2026, a day after settlers violently seized Palestinian homes in the neighborhood. Photo by Katrine Dige Houmøller for Drop Site News. JERICHO, Occupied West Bank--"They beat all of us. Children, women, and men," Mustafa Kaaba said, standing on a dusty street in the city of Jericho in the occupied West Bank. The night before, November 4, armed Israeli settlers burst into his home and the homes of his neighbors, ransacking them, violently forcing the families out, and warning them not to return. Kaaba clutched his head and struggled to lift his arm, which was visibly swollen and bruised after settlers beat him with sticks. Around him, his family's belongings lay scattered across the street. Kaaba's pregnant wife, Fatima, gathered what was left of their clothes and stuffed them into plastic bags. After being expelled from their home, the family of seven was forced to sleep in their car and on the street. "They ripped up the children's schoolbooks and books written in Arabic," Fatima told Drop Site. "They didn't even leave our children anything to study with." Fatima said the settlers took their refrigerator, washing machine, television, and entire bedroom set to another apartment seized by the settlers. Around her, children ran between piles of rubble and scattered sheep that wandered out from a nearby corrugated metal shed. The couple's young daughter had been in a playful mood, running up to people for hugs. Then, without warning, she burst into tears, screaming and running away from those around her. Her father tried in vain to comfort her. "She is having a panic attack," Kaaba said. "I think it's triggered by the trauma from last night." The family is now afraid to walk around Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta, their neighborhood on the outskirts of the city. "It's dangerous, even just getting to the end of this street. I swear, it's dangerous. What if they come after us?" Kaaba said. "We don't have anything left." Fatima stood nearby clutching a piece of clothing. "Our house is still standing, but they told us not to come back," she added. "They say it belongs to them now." LEFT: Mustafa Kaaba and Fatima Kaaba's children look through the belongings of their home in Jericho after Israeli settlers stormed the family's home the previous night and forced them out. RIGHT: Mustafa and Fatima Kaaba's youngest child looks through her empty schoolbag shortly before suffering a panic attack, which her father attributed to the previous night's raid, in Jericho, occupied West Bank. November 5, 2026. Photos by Katrine Dige Houmøller for Drop Site News. According to residents, at least 13 Palestinian households were driven from their homes in Jericho by some 30 Israeli settlers, some of them masked, who rampaged through the neighborhood. The next morning, the settlers made their occupation known. They hung Israeli flags from the balconies and entrances of multiple houses--a standard marker of a Palestinian home taken over by settlers. Armed men patrolled between the newly occupied homes--with rifles slung over their shoulders or pistols tucked into their waistbands. Israeli women and children wandered along the gravel roads. Young men sat outside reading the Torah while gunmen stood guard at every property. The expansion of Israeli settlements and outposts across the occupied West Bank over the past three years has been rapid and increasingly violent. More than 6,400 Palestinians, including over 3,100 children, were displaced between January 2023 and August 2026 as a result of settler attacks and restrictions on access to their land, to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs. At least 48 Palestinian communities were completely emptied of their residents during that period. Even in that context, the takeover by Israeli settlers of homes inside a Palestinian city in the occupied West Bank represents a dangerous escalation in Israel's dispossession of Palestinians across the territory. Some Palestinians are comparing it to the situation in Hebron, the largest city in the West Bank and the only one to have Israeli settlements inside the heart of the city. Most Israeli settlements surround Palestinian towns and cities, usually on the surrounding hilltops, but in Hebron armed Israeli settlers live in the midst of Palestinian residents and are guarded by a permanent and large deployment of Israeli troops, making Hebron one of the most and ethnically segregated urban areas in the West Bank with Palestinians even prevented from walking down certain streets. "Establishing a settlement inside Jericho poses a security threat and constitutes a geopolitical disaster that must not be allowed to happen. This move is designed to deepen friction and violence, entrench an apartheid regime, and foreclose any possibility of a future political agreement," the Israeli group Peace Now, that organizes against settlements in the West Bank, warned in a . The violent home seizures on Wednesday came after a gradual buildup. The neighborhood of Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta had been experiencing repeated attacks by settlers, often from a nearby outpost called Palace Farms, according to Peace Now. Settlers also demolished around 13 homes in the area in February and again in July. Rubble is still scattered throughout the neighborhood. By October 27, the day of the Israeli elections, settlers had already begun fencing off parts of the neighborhood and installing infrastructure, according to Peace Now, which also reported a number of break-ins, thefts, and assaults on residents. A gate was erected to block access to an entire street, cutting off dozens of Palestinian homes. Now, the settlers have taken over some of those homes. The Israeli military did nothing to stop the violent takeover, with multiple Palestinian residents telling Drop Site that troops stood by as families were forced out. The following morning, Israeli military vehicles repeatedly drove through the neighborhood. Uniformed soldiers warmly greeted the settlers, shook hands, and embraced them. Some entered the occupied houses, appearing familiar with the settlers inside. Outside one of the newly occupied properties, a settler sat in a chair keeping guard. "They're good friends of the families now," he said as soldiers walked into the house. "Since last night," he added. LEFT: Israeli settlers move into Palestinian homes in Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta neighborhood of Jericho, in the occupied West Bank, on November 5, 2026. RIGHT: Israeli soldiers visit Israeli settler families throughout the day in Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta neighborhood of Jericho, in the occupied West Bank, after the settlers occupied several homes in the Palestinian city the previous night. Photos by Katrine Dige Houmøller for Drop Site News. The properties are located on the outskirts of Jericho and technically in Area C--a designation under the Oslo Accords of the 1990s where Israel retains full civil and military control--right on the border of Area A, where the Palestinian Authority has nominal security and civil control, and where most of Jericho city is located. The takeover was reportedly coordinated by the settlement organization Nachala and the Binyamin Regional Council. Both organizations claim that the properties were legally purchased. Jericho Governor Hussein Hamayel disputed the claims, saying in an interview with Raya Media Network that the land belongs to Jordan's state treasury and describing the alleged sales as forged. In response to an inquiry from Drop Site, about the Israeli military's role in the takeover, accounts of violence and looting by settlers, and the settlers' continued occupation of the Palestinian homes, a military official said in a written response that "Upon the entry of Israeli civilians into homes in the area adjacent to Jericho, situational assessments and field patrols were conducted to examine the incident. In the coming week, the examination of the settlers' claims regarding the purchase of the lands will continue." The official also said "the action was carried out without prior coordination or approval from the IDF." They added, "The mission of the soldiers stationed at the military outpost in the area is to safeguard the security of all residents in the area and to prevent terror and additional confrontations." Yet following the Israeli settlers' takeover of the homes, the Jericho neighborhood is increasingly off limits to Palestinians or perceived supporters. The morning after the attacks, settlers in an ATV recklessly chased Palestinian journalists through the streets, relentlessly pursuing them until they managed to escape the area. Mahmoud Faridat, a resident of Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta, owns two farms directly adjacent to the newly occupied properties. The following morning, Faridat went to herd his sheep inside one of the farms with his brother, Jamal, and his nephew. They were stopped by settlers, who beat Jamal and the nephew and sprayed them with tear gas, Faridat said. Settlers had also erected another makeshift barrier, arranging chairs and wooden planks across the road to block access to Faridat's farmland. "[A settler] told us not to go through it, but our water ponds and farm are all in front of the house," Faridat told Drop Site immediately after failing to reach his land. "From the moment they [the settlers] came, they have attacked us." Even the main roads in the neighborhood have become dangerous. "The street we're standing on now is still accessible, even though the army stops us to ask questions," Faridat said. "But tomorrow, Allah knows, they may not let us pass at all." HEADLINES: Progressive Earthquake | Senate Shockwaves | House Power Bloc |
Flipping Red Seats | Downballot Dominance | Beating Big Money | Time to
Deliver Change | & MORE!
★ ★ ★
[1]PROGRESSIVE EARTHQUAKE POWERS BLUE TSUNAMI multi-candidate collage
The Blue Tsunami that crushed the GOP Tuesday night — powered by a
Progressive Earthquake. Our movement brought the grassroots energy and the
bold agenda that mobilized millions of voters to repudiate Trump and MAGA
once and for all.
This cycle, Our Revolution made over 5 MILLION voter contacts to elect
over 142 PROGRESSIVE CHAMPIONS at every level of government! We took back
the House and Senate, flipped a TON of red seats with economic populists,
and elected a new generation of progressive state and city officials.
THANK YOU to all our organizers, volunteers, and grassroots donors who
helped us prove once again that deep organizing can beat Big Money.
For a decade, the establishment told us that Progressives couldn't win in
swing states, couldn't win in red districts, and couldn't build a
governing majority.
Well, look at the map now.
[2]2026 Midterms red and blue U.S. congressional election map screenshot
All the work we did to win a progressive wave in the primaries set the
stage for this historic general election victory. We built the bench,
expanded the map, and proved that bold working-class politics can win.
As Our Revolution Executive Director Joseph Geevarghese told [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40009?t=1011&akid=11563%2E5885482%2ESbTntV ]Common
Dreams: "The blue wave was powered by a progressive wave. We are the
center of gravity in this party, and we intend to drive the agenda."
[4]Common Dreams article screenshot on progressive mandate after blue
tsunami
But with this new power comes enormous responsibility. The grassroots led
this victory. Now the grassroots must lead the Democratic Party in a new
progressive direction. [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40010?t=1012&akid=11563%2E5885482%2ESbTntV ]Now it’s time to deliver.
This edition of the Rev Report tells about how our grassroots movement
made history — and where we go from here.
★ ★ ★
SENATE SHOCKWAVES: A NEW ERA OF PROGRESSIVE POWER
TEXAS. MAINE. MICHIGAN. Three states. Three extraordinary Senate
victories. And three powerful examples of what happens when Our
Revolution’s grassroots organizing meets bold progressive leadership.
TROY JACKSON — MAINE
[6]Man at Maine campaign podium with Jackson campaign banner partly
visible
When the political establishment tried to control the process of replacing
Graham Platner, Our Revolution helped ensure the new Senate candidate was
an Our Revolution-backed candidate.
We mobilized hundreds of our members to show up at county Democratic
caucus meetings and helped nominate Troy Jackson, a former logger, union
leader, and working-class champion who knows what it's like to take on
powerful interests.
Then we went all in — mobilizing 300,000 calls, texts, and emails to help
Troy defeat longtime Republican Sen. Susan Collins!
★ ★ ★
ABDUL EL-SAYED — MICHIGAN
[7]Candidate speaking at THANK YOU MICHIGAN / ABDUL FOR SENATE podium
Our organizing work is sending a doctor, public health champion, and
unapologetic fighter for Medicare for All to the U.S. Senate!
Our Revolution backed Abdul El-Sayed throughout his primary and mobilized
all the way through Election Night, making over 330,000 voter contacts to
help deliver this historic victory in a critical swing state.
His message was simple and powerful: Money out of politics. Money in your
pocket. Medicare for All. Because of our organizing, our movement sent
Washington the same message about the kind of change we're demanding.
★ ★ ★
JAMES TALARICO — TEXAS
[8]Speaker at LOVE THY NEIGHBOR podium with cheering supporters
TEXAS TURNED BLUE!
Our Revolution first backed James Talarico in 2018 when he first ran for
State Rep. as part of our work to build a progressive candidate
pipeline in the Lone Star State. This year, we supported him again as he
delivered a stunning 12-POINT Senate victory in Texas, changing the
landscape of what's politically possible!
This wasn't just a Senate flip. It was a breakthrough for our progressive
movement in a state where Our Revolution’s grassroots organizers have been
in the trenches to build power for over a decade.
And as you'll see below, the Texas story didn't stop at the top of the
ticket!
★ ★ ★
A NEW PROGRESSIVE POWER BLOC IS HEADED TO CONGRESS!
[9]New House Progressives multi-candidate collage
In addition to building power in the Senate, we're adding DOZENS of new
progressive leaders to the U.S. House — and the establishment's tired
electability argument is crumbling before our eyes.
Our Revolution candidates did not run away from progressive values - they
embodied them. They are organizers, union champions, and young
working-class fighters who ran on making life better for ordinary working
people - including Melat Kiros (CO-1), Claire Valdez (NY-7), and Darializa
Avila Chevalier (NY-13).
Many came up through the progressive candidate pipeline Our Revolution has
spent a decade building, including Aisha Wahab (CA-14) and Chris
Rabb (PA-3).
[10]Outdoor campaign event with AISHA sign at lectern
Our Revolution has been organizing with Aisha for years - helping her win
races from Hayward City Council to the California State Senate, and now to
Congress. In this cycle, Our Revolution mobilized 300,000 voter
contacts to help Aisha beat back millions in AIPAC spending against her.
Our Revolution also has a long history with Chris Rabb - we endorsed him
when he first ran for PA State Rep in 2016, supported him as he passed
ground-breaking state legislation, and this year organized to help him win
a seat in Congress representing Philadelphia.
Examples like Aisha and Chris prove that Our Revolution’s goal of
investing in long-term progressive political infrastructure pays off!
★ ★ ★
🚨 WE FLIPPED RED SEATS PROGRESSIVE BLUE!
[11]Six-person red seats flipped progressive blue composite graphic
In race after race, Our Revolution proved that organizing the grassroots
around a bold progressive agenda can WIN IN MAGA TERRITORY! Here’s a few
examples:
In the Rio Grande Valley of Texas, Our Revolution made over 59,000 voter
contacts to help Katy Padilla Stout (TX 23) pull off an extraordinary flip
to replace disgraced GOP Rep. Tony Gonzales after being largely overlooked
by the Democratic establishment.
In California’s Central Valley, Our Phonebank Team made over 5000 calls to
help Randy Villegas (CA-22) trounce GOP incumbent David Valadao.
And in Michigan, we made 63,000 voter contacts to help Will Lawrence, a
former Sunrise Movement cofounder, defeat GOP incumbent Tom Barrett.
We also helped several working class champions defeat MAGA candidates,
including Bob Brooks (Pennsylvania), a union firefighter, Brian Poindexter
(Ohio), union ironworker, and Sam Forstag (Montana), a former wildland
firefighter
Our movement is expanding the map to MAGA territory and demonstrating that
working-class politics reach voters everywhere.
★ ★ ★
STATE POWER: THE PROGRESSIVE WAVE GOES DEEPER!
The progressive earthquake didn't stop in Washington.
Our Revolution’s deep grassroots organizing also won key state-level races
across America, including:
[12]Person in tan cowboy hat speaking at Our Revolution Organize to Win
event
TEXAS: Our Revolution made over 244,000 voter contacts for State Rep.
Vikki Goodwin, who defeated rightwing incumbent Dan Patrick for Lt.
Governor. And, we supported former Our Revolution organizer Clayton
Tucker in his bid for TX Agriculture Commissioner — following in the
footsteps of Our Revolution Board member and populist rabblerouser Jim
Hightower!
MISSOURI: Our Revolution reached over 155,000 voters to elect a
Progressive Slate of 16 State House and Senate candidates to break the
Republican supermajority in the state legislature!
[13]Speaker standing at MI DEMS podium with Michigan Democratic Party
banner
MICHIGAN: We mobilized thousands of voters to elect Eli Savit, a
previously Our Revolution-endorsed County Prosecutor, as the state’s next
Attorney General.
MINNESOTA: Our Revolution supported Attorney General Keith Ellison in his
race to win reelection, continuing his work on consumer protection and
corporate accountability.
VERMONT: We helped Molly Gray flip the lieutenant governor's office blue,
adding another progressive victory to the national wave!
These victories are strategic for Our Revolution because so much of the
fight for affordable housing, workers' rights, environmental protection,
and corporate accountability happens at the state level.
★ ★ ★
FROM CITY HALL TO CAPITOL HILL: A NEW GENERATION RISES
Some of the most exciting breakthroughs came in America's cities, where
Our Revolution activists on the ground are helping a new generation of
progressive leaders step into power.
[14]Woman speaking at microphone with supporters at event
Our Revolution’s grassroots organizing continues to add to the ranks of
new progressive mayors like NYC’s Zohran Mamdani, including victories by
David Morales in Providence, RI, democratic socialist Janeese Lewis George
in DC, and former city councilwoman Nithya Raman in Los Angeles!
Our local victories are putting progressive leaders in the role of CEO of
our cities, giving us a testing ground to prove that progressive policies
work to improve people’s lives at the level of government closest to them.
★ ★ ★
BALLOT MEASURES: TAKING ON BIG MONEY AND DEFENDING WORKERS
[15]Red MONEY OUT OF POLITICS sign with MapUpMichigan.org
Some of the most consequential victories weren't for candidates at all.
They were grassroots-driven ballot initiatives for structural reforms that
can reshape our democracy.
MICHIGAN: GET BIG MONEY OUT OF POLITICS!
Our Revolution backed Michigan’s winning campaign-finance reform measure
which restricts certain political contributions from regulated utilities
and large government contractors while expanding disclosure requirements.
This is the template Our Revolution wants to take state by state —
challenging dark and corporate money and making elections more accountable
to the people.
[16]Vermont YES ON 3 green license-plate-style campaign graphic
VERMONT: WORKERS' RIGHTS IN THE CONSTITUTION!
Our Revolution helped pass Vermont’s Proposal 3, which enshrines the right
of employees to organize and join unions for collective bargaining in the
state constitution!
It's a significant victory for organized labor and an example of how
voters can establish protections that extend beyond any single election
cycle.
★ ★ ★
CORRUPTION IN THE CROSSHAIRS
[17]UPROOT CORRUPTION red and blue text graphic
One of the biggest stories of this election? Corruption became a
kitchen-table issue.
The Iran War, the Epstein Files, corporate greed, sky high prices, Trump’s
family cashing in on crypto schemes, big money trying to buy our elections
— it’s all tied together by CORRUPTION.
As Our Revolution leader Joseph Geevarghese told [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40011?t=1013&akid=11563%2E5885482%2ESbTntV ]Huffington Post:
"People see the quid pro quo in action. They see donors lining up to get
returns on their investments, while they feel the economic strain
themselves — and it disgusts the electorate."
[19]HuffPost screenshot on corruption as an electoral issue
Affordability and accountability aren't separate fights. They're two sides
of the same coin.
That's why Our Revolution is doubling down on the fight to get big money
out of politics, uproot corruption, take on corporate greed, and make
government work for the people who actually keep this country running.
The election sent an unmistakable message. Now Congress has to answer it.
★ ★ ★
WE BEAT BIG MONEY!
[20]Forbes screenshot with Elon Musk and headline on $458 million midterm
spending
This was the most expensive midterm in history. More than $5 BILLION was
flushed down the drain trying to elect Republicans.
Elon Musk alone poured nearly HALF A BILLION DOLLARS into the election —
but it didn’t stop the progressive wave!
Millions of Americans organized, volunteered, knocked doors, made calls,
sent texts, and turned out to vote. And Our Revolution exceeded our 5
MILLION voter contact goal and engaged more than 50,000 activists.
[21]Group of grassroots organizers outdoors holding campaign signs
This is how we build power that lasts beyond Election Day. [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/40010?t=1014&akid=11563%2E5885482%2ESbTntV ]Chip in a
donation to help us replenish our resources for the fight to come!
★ ★ ★
FROM THE BALLOT BOX TO CAPITOL HILL: THE FIGHT CONTINUES!
One of the biggest reasons Our Revolution helped win this election is
simple: We organize year-round, not just when there's an election around
the corner.
Now we're preparing to bring that same grassroots energy directly to
Congress.
We'll be ramping up our Capitol Hill actions, organizing virtual lobby
visits, and mobilizing members to push for action on affordability,
accountability, and structural reform.

Because of our organizing, our movement sent Washington the same message about the kind of change we're demanding. ★ ★ ★ JAMES TALARICO — TEXAS [8]Speaker at LOVE THY NEIGHBOR podium with cheering supporters TEXAS TURNED BLUE! _Nadia was only 15 years old when they went looking for her. _ A pastor had called House Parent Project, a children's home in Mexico. He knew Nadia was in danger. He even knew the Metro station in Mexico City where she could often be found.So the house parents went and they found her. But to understand what happened next, you need to know where Nadia came from. She never knew her father. Her mother lived an unstable and dangerous life, moving from one man to another. Nadia was the oldest of three little girls. Her youngest sister was given up for adoption. But Nadia grew up with almost nothing and no one. She survived on the streets of Mexico City, surrounded by drugs, prostitution, abandonment, and exploitation. Imagine being 15 years old and wondering if there is a single adult in this world you can trust. That was the girl they found near that Metro station. There was doubt in Nadia's eyes. But they asked her to give them a chance.
---
[ Help Feed And Protect A Child](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=ff4230e56f5f474baddbddb193f28ae2&_e=YbXlL1ZiflyQSzZ3mHOGuznpRUl9ayJg1SctCKfPKqhy1EARv9gVRXmgVpK0I-VY_ZeEfYIiCAlQ-wlF7E7A_9KYELNS7olVhFSo3N_gGUb29GHHFnKS5yBUGwzy5TRQ7qkCrTeogy-MV31hTEjP548QEmVan3_GAdrCfxHUuxLs_dGsPnEfJjDeIlHHIBhNSx9rmrMwTpBYCHOsByE8zmlZ-lFLeA0RQbPsS4vayHdSiZ353H7k2wwbBU9C3nWsjb-xuu29F84Ioi2ajvqzYObbhR2VN6o3aENOm3fHU-mBbO6t82gIPTBSbRGpxl679_woxe2HgxfiC20SVUrnQJtQs_mnfQF7yqVXVWuizOSpflpEPq2lbMRTYEUZBxJXTDJStf9q-oLEUFaPhreJWd-85V1vuoNOInlvUH-XttJhBQ-ILRp-h99m4GOWBfp7s2oC40uwD4LYbslF78ASRwilaRFsb-7DYg8r2FQSNqucyE325hDOaIRVHzXy3g-iGP4wbf3v1WNthkzXq9CfOc6AIPHkK1XH2q3u_T8aFP1ORWzjxPkZiQrAW5BH60TGs03Kn61fzqjszK0ZF4YVS9HFRUFQM7WCD26wykLwI07TPUhSggrCn8Sv1Y5fRRAxCZeUuLGANXFwAe7mu9sY3khm7S1V66juSjnj_4HRdrs%3D)

They told her something every child deserves to hear: **You are loved. **They promised to protect her and help her get an education. And Nadia willingly went with them. She left behind a horrible life and came home to parents who would raise her as their own. Peter, Nadia's story is one reason **Sound of Freedom Foundation** works with groups like House Parent Project.My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the movie _Sound of Freedom_ because after learning what traffickers do to innocent children, I could not simply look away.For me, it stopped being a movie. It became a calling. Today, the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** carries that mission forward. Our mission is simple: **Stop the sale of God 's children.** House Parent Project shares that commitment. Their house parents give these children the love and care they've never known.
---
[ Help Feed And Protect A Child](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=ff4230e56f5f474baddbddb193f28ae2&_e=YbXlL1ZiflyQSzZ3mHOGuznpRUl9ayJg1SctCKfPKqhy1EARv9gVRXmgVpK0I-VY_ZeEfYIiCAlQ-wlF7E7A_9KYELNS7olVhFSo3N_gGUb29GHHFnKS5yBUGwzy5TRQ7qkCrTeogy-MV31hTEjP548QEmVan3_GAdrCfxHUuxLs_dGsPnEfJjDeIlHHIBhNSx9rmrMwTpBYCHOsByE8zmlZ-lFLeA0RQbPsS4vayHfzN5SAI-_crbaCJhlndUrnBvwTwWtBNB3Eqn-o4bJKkkiqBWfcaYDx_j8LECwV50CufPH8arDnErOB4gG8GqQtc80mUOOjJEpuOrF16BKqyjCG8IICK7IVdlh6UmiEnxmTn0zxeNvHR8H9DYyh3-GnNNyDPAKIXHX3WYXUGeJZh7ubSUQwCObw00bf0ZOgNnf6IvmJ-rITz9v4nTUG_fXr4x1n1Cl1Rk8MRN0r3oMz3J3-y4B4Kj8ukX6EHrYJcyfjT-jgDODqdZl6QL9QaBiR8urgQ6aY41uWLZc5MwoAlDCQA4t3QAddkbM4g-iyZePHYxkowQmSA4AUWALWG_kTR-WkYlzOxlJdaSYeA49HbGJIuc3A5itsbdz5yES_NYtL295eiBQ4LmSd6Fx9zYsbU9sFwPXBXxkzZ9fVfTrK7OjZewMFjIUT6xk9V7mJjPA%3D)

And Nadia shows what can happen when a child is not abandoned. A couple of years after her rescue, the team found Nadia's sister, Sofia. She was suffering through many of the same horrors. They rescued her too. Today, Sofia works full time caring for other children who have experienced the same kinds of brokenness. Then something beautiful happened in Nadia's life. She met Joseph, who had also grown up in the same Village - the House Parent Project community. They fell in love. They married, Joseph became a foreman, and the couple moved away for several years. They welcomed a son and daughter of their own. Yet they kept coming back for Christmas, Mother's Day, and birthdays. **Their hearts were still with the children. **Finally, in 2019, Nadia and Joseph came home permanently. Today, **they are second in command at one of the large children 's homes**. The child who once needed someone to find her**grew up to help care for children who need to be found. **That is**restoration**. That is **hope**. And that is why I am writing to you. Today, House Parent Project cares for, educates and protects **between 130 and 150 children in two homes, every single day**.

This week's election could appear from the view of future history as a [sea change](https://substack.com/redirect/0b894dca-89dd-4db9-b6dd-6ea8f769750e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in U.S. politics. Or it [could](https://substack.com/redirect/41192731-147d-4d63-81f2-18482c3b0175?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) appear as the [continuation](https://substack.com/@teodelnorte/note/c-378870613) of a [pattern](https://substack.com/redirect/78ae7614-4075-4c7f-89e0-f943ce961e57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that has gone on too long. Several voices have written this week to encourage Democrats, as they retake congressional leadership in both the upper and lower houses next year, to be bold and swing for the proverbial fence.

This article explores some ways that Democrats can take advantage of the next Congress to hold corruption accountable, respond to continuing social and environmental crises, and prevent the recurring cyclical electoral losses that have typically resulted from elected officials failing to faithfully champion the interests of their constituents and supporters after winning elections.
### **Limits**
Democrats in the next Congress will enjoy [at least](https://substack.com/redirect/a67e85c6-5bc7-4181-8d7c-54b141a5bd17?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a 4-seat majority in the Senate and a 41-seat majority in the House. Those leads could grow marginally even further.
Those majorities will be enough to constitute a majority in each chamber, but not enough to overcome a presidential veto.
Unable to move his agenda through Congress as he did over the past two years, the president will likely make frequent use of that veto over the rest of his term to impede Congress. As a result, any visionary bills passed by the incoming majorities will need to be resuscitated in a future Congress in order to ever see the light of day.
But that doesn't mean that Congress has to settle for stagnancy until 2028. Unless Democrats use their other congressional powers assertively, they will likely invite Republicans to recover their recent losses in 2028.

### **Opportunities**
In the next Congress, Democrats will enjoy crucial opportunities to use the congressional oversight process, both to expose corruption and also to identify problems to then later fix in legislation. There are gaps across the federal government left in the wake of the [unconstitutional DOGE cuts](https://substack.com/redirect/3e0ec9ed-264c-4119-b9df-26ae8625e7dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) implemented perversely by the world's richest man, all of which present an attack surface for oversight.
**Melting ICE** needs to be an urgent priority, both to respond to a mounting humanitarian crisis, and also to avoid betraying the grassroots communities that pushed Democrats back into control of Congress.
In addition to leveraging the oversight process to, for instance, hold hearings about [violence committed by ICE agents](https://substack.com/redirect/e100f9ee-0d6b-4989-ad02-12f8688fba2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during their various deployments around the country, Democrats in Congress can also hold the agency accountable by shrinking it. Every DHS funding bill should diminish the ICE budget, while funding an alternative agency to take on customs enforcement while ICE is phased out of immigration enforcement and then shut down.
Senator-Elect Peggy Flanagan from Minnesota will soon become the first Native American U.S. Senator. Setting aside the influence of her identity (to which I'll return below), she has been quite assertive in her [rhetoric](https://substack.com/@naomiklein/note/c-379914863?r=97w99) about wanting to curtail ICE, as well as her [support](https://substack.com/redirect/78f06968-e9a9-4564-b6a9-a1e2eb4008d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the grassroots organizing that made Minneapolis grassroots [leaders](https://substack.com/redirect/0b809d26-a075-4e82-a8aa-6fcf4fc33656?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the rest of the country.
I hope that her voice, along with El-Syed's, might prove persuasive to their colleagues who appear poised to [yet again conciliate](https://substack.com/@extremearturo/note/c-380315188?r=97w99&utm_medium=ios&utm_source=notes-share-action) with the establishment, conferring false legitimacy on a rogue agency that remains [younger](https://substack.com/redirect/3f755aba-822e-4eda-ad33-f18f3761788d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than many of its staff.
In particular, Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee are [calling for](https://substack.com/@extremearturo/note/c-380315188?r=97w99) ICE body cameras, which some still imagine to be a step forward in spite of evidence and warnings stretching back over a decade. Too many forget that [body cameras are state surveillance devices](https://substack.com/redirect/ea43dd8d-2e0a-4d1a-9700-e07f7ce8716a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--not accountability instruments.
This isn't just about failing to go far enough. House Democrats still appear inclined to keep rolling back the clock.

Congressional hearings could also offer Democrats a chance to publicly probe **the Epstein files** , as well as **the Trump family 's self-enrichment in public office**. That is not a new position for me: I wrote nearly a decade ago, during his first term, that [impeachment--specifically for corruption](https://substack.com/redirect/2da11c80-810f-44c5-92b5-24c90d48db1d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--was the key to holding the president accountable.
The analysis applies even more strongly now than when I first wrote that argument in 2019. It's also the principal reason why I favor Rep. Jamie (D-MD) to be the next Speaker of the House. He has confirmed that, as the manager of the impeachment processes under Trump's first term, he wanted to include Emoluments Clause violations in the charges--but was stopped by the Speaker of the House at the time, who perversely [got credit from the press](https://substack.com/redirect/8440a447-0531-43b2-bc45-6e0902556bc1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for an impeachment process that she [hamstrung](https://substack.com/redirect/531e3730-74f0-4a11-abb1-41535c5d241f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from the outset.
**Climate vulnerability & resilience** are further areas in dire need of congressional attention. An [informed Congress](https://substack.com/redirect/156b05f3-35ae-4e28-a4fd-aa5d4c63b8b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) could better fashion legislation responding to the scale of the [growing needs](https://substack.com/redirect/4b50cdae-92bd-4d54-8d92-4eac6c968c6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) around the country, while hearings exploring climate resiliency opportunities could help crystallize the political will for transformative solutions in the next Congress. There is no policy area that matters more to the future than climate justice.
When I ran for Congress half a decade ago, progressives [spent a lot of time](https://substack.com/redirect/975a731e-143a-4b2d-a34b-c53dd325548a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) debating how to force a public discussion of **universal healthcare** as an alternative to a corporate healthcare system driving people to early graves en masse in order to maximize profits. While Democratic party leaders at the time were [entirely unwilling](https://substack.com/redirect/2a21975f-d7a6-4798-a2d0-909af6d9bbb9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to even countenance the possibility of even a mere hearing, a Congress largely limited to oversight presents a perfect opportunity to investigate and publicize the healthcare crisis, ideally with an eye toward crafting a transformative proposal to fix it.
### **The Pentagon**
Oversight of the **military procurement** process also presents opportunities for public accountability and exposing corruption. I have long railed about the military's failure to ever complete an audit, which has never been defensible in any way.

[Sometimes reality offers irony that exceeds any fiction.](https://substack.com/redirect/11098729-fbe1-46ed-b7ce-17f4ea45a0b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
