But the Pentagon may be more vulnerable to public scrutiny in this current moment than it has been at any point since the end (maybe even the beginning) of the Cold War.
The failures of a decades-long military strategy based entirely on expensive corporate weapon systems have recently been [demonstrated](https://substack.com/redirect/0e46f752-40ab-453d-a4b3-70994cf9731b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the [world to see](https://substack.com/redirect/602b6164-9801-4954-9c49-66394b1cb206?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The U.S. has lost over [100 aircraft worth $4 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/b698463c-12c6-419a-8a7b-578a918b5608?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) alone, setting aside the [extensive damage](https://substack.com/redirect/2cb2b90a-8130-4619-8b50-c0abb7811df3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to bases around the Gulf that effectively forced the [retreat](https://substack.com/redirect/eff59d69-12ee-43f2-b7dc-b12ac5f5ab27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the Fifth Fleet.
Rather than continue to sign blank checks to Lockheed Martin and Raytheon, Congress should explore and publicly expose the [corruption](https://substack.com/redirect/11098729-fbe1-46ed-b7ce-17f4ea45a0b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that has long fueled the military industrial complex whose creator [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/1aefee13-e7a1-484d-86ef-f66b1b436335?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--over 60 years ago--would threaten democracy in America.
Oversight is also crucial to identify and remove the politicized hacks placed in the Pentagon by Hegseth to replace the many experienced, [professional commanders who he fired](https://substack.com/redirect/64ac7e66-a8cc-4949-957e-74ed4739e880?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Removing a politicized Secretary of Defense will not be enough to weed out his continuing institutional influence, in the same way that removing presidents doesn't remove the judges who they appoint for life.
But whereas judges are granted to have lifetime appointments, the military is supposed to be apolitical--meaning that Congress has a mandate to remove & replace Hegseth's cronies and restore the institutional capacity of the Judge Advocate General (JAG) Corps to enable courts-martial where appropriate. Navy [Admiral Brad Cooper](https://substack.com/redirect/aee329c1-9d94-4ae1-9192-fbeed6cfb36c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who served as Hegseth's lead planner of the War on Iran, and was ultimately responsible for the attack that [killed 120 Iranian schoolchildren](https://substack.com/redirect/5f49b1d2-05e1-46cb-8db1-075ac62e41bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the first day of the war, should be at the top of the list.
Beyond Cooper, any senior military commander promoted by Hegseth should be presumptively suspect, and Pentagon funds should be restricted by Congress until Hegseth's appointees are replaced by less politicized, more professionalized and experienced figures. If the last year taught us anything, it must be that the professionalism of the military must be guarded at all costs, if only to prevent it from becoming a tool for repression.
Many writers were [asking](https://substack.com/redirect/ce27853a-1879-4106-acd7-9db562c7a00b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the last several weeks--and some might still remain curious-- whether the military would enable, or instead stand up to, a president who openly violates the Constitution. We know the answer, because that's [been happening](https://substack.com/redirect/e100f9ee-0d6b-4989-ad02-12f8688fba2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for years.
I would love to see the Pentagon shrunk into oblivion. The world will be a more peaceful place when that happens.
Recognizing the current political reality, a purge meant to de-politicize the institution would be a compelling place to begin.

That process has already [begun](https://substack.com/redirect/7fbe4c2a-751d-4399-a745-1bd179d07c68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the Department of Justice, which has also been hollowed out by dismissals and departures under the politicized administration of Trump appointees.
I worked in Washington over the second term of George W. Bush, when a [similar dynamic](https://substack.com/redirect/2cc6bc89-62fa-40ec-97a5-e8031390a656?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) eroded the capacity of DOJ to perform its longstanding missions of protecting, among other things, voting rights and the environment alongside criminal prosecutions and defending the government in civil cases. It takes time to restore, but aggressive oversight can help lay the foundation for that process under the next administration.
Congress could also restrict DOJ funding until the Department, for instance, prosecutes ICE agents who have publicly committed lethal violence but escaped federal accountability. It's worth noting here how, perhaps inspired by their constituents' [assertive activism](https://substack.com/redirect/0b809d26-a075-4e82-a8aa-6fcf4fc33656?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), state & local leaders have [stepped forward](https://substack.com/redirect/c7c1c8e9-7ef5-4a24-992b-4e04e55275f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to pursue the justice that their federal counterparts have stonewalled.
As long as the federal DOJ remains co-opted by the president as his personal law firm, Congress should diminish its capacity by reducing the Department's budget.
In any case, as long as we have a military, we need its leaders to understand the ethical and [legal responsibilities](https://substack.com/redirect/5b729493-47ba-40d5-90ad-80aad839ae8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) they will share for [following orders](https://substack.com/redirect/86ded0cb-c262-459e-90f1-693e6017e060?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that ultimately violate human rights. If executive branch or military agencies are ordered to take action in secret, or when Congress makes itself complicit (as it tends to do), [dissent from the inside](https://substack.com/redirect/8c8decc0-14b8-4dc7-bb20-0fe063516ce8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--either from command positions or publicly, as [whistleblowers](https://substack.com/redirect/19742f80-9397-40ae-99c0-c783cfadb2a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--can be the last remaining check and balance protecting We the People of the United States.
### **Leadership**
The very first test of the Democratically-controlled Congress will be over its leadership choices.
If elected Democrats defer to the established corporate leadership of their respective caucuses embodied in Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY) and Rep. Hakeem Jefferies (D-NY), they will likely end up dithering as a result, shifting deck chairs on the Titanic of the United States over the next congressional term until they lose so much public support that they fumble an easily winnable 2028 election and cede it to a right wing hack. Sound [familiar](https://substack.com/redirect/78ae7614-4075-4c7f-89e0-f943ce961e57?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)?
If, instead, the incoming majority choose new leaders sensitive to the concerns of voters from across the political spectrum--including universal healthcare, climate justice, and holding corruption accountable--Democrats in Washington will have a chance over the next two years to note only meaningfully shift the dial, but build on their recent successes in the next election cycle.
The continuing failures of the past [ensure](https://substack.com/redirect/d4716b59-cf1e-46fc-83d4-878e94458852?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) any [number](https://substack.com/redirect/4b50cdae-92bd-4d54-8d92-4eac6c968c6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of [future](https://substack.com/redirect/156b05f3-35ae-4e28-a4fd-aa5d4c63b8b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) crises, but many opportunities remain to contain how severe these crises will grow.
Thankfully, more than half a dozen incoming Democratic senators have [pledged not to support Schumer](https://substack.com/redirect/7145d7a8-1547-4b03-902c-612c362184e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). They're not nearly enough to force new leadership, no one has yet emerged to challenge Schumer, and Congress remains [dominated](https://substack.com/redirect/1f3e2a8c-d228-4fc6-9464-c117950aa06e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by AIPAC--all of which might seem to render Schumer comfortably ensconced.
That said, the election was less than a week ago, and we still have over two months left to build momentum against Schumer & the old guard of [congressional fossils](https://substack.com/redirect/67d55eab-f7fb-4ae4-ac71-467d5445a305?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Now that the election is behind us, I encourage readers to help make sure that every incoming Democrat hears that their constituents want new leadership within the party.
_Help build support for new leadership in Congress by sharing this post with your friends._
[ Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1018597&post_id=223827585&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIzODI3NTg1LCJpYXQiOjE3OTQwNjY1MjAsImV4cCI6MTc5NjY1ODUyMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTEwMTg1OTciLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.ZfuFwdTPNdOHqj7boIfHQv7Jf4yykRuKugla_Uha7e0)
It's also interesting to observe the seeming centrality of New York City in the default choice among congressional leaders. While Schumer represents the entire State of New York as a Senator, his support base is concentrated in NYC, and he & Jeffries are both products of its political machine.
When I ran for Congress half a decade ago, the most politically powerful part of the country was on the other side of it. San Francisco was represented then by both the Speaker of the House and the Vice President, as well as the senior California Senator.
On the one hand, I'm not averse to NYC being the political center of the country. NYC is, after all, more a melting pot than most of the U.S. But why are the particular voices from New York who want to dominate Washington among its most conservative?
### **Representation**
Friends keep asking me about Senator-Elect Abdul El-Syed in Michigan, who is poised to become the country's first Muslim senator. On the one hand, while other voices celebrate [increased diversity](https://substack.com/redirect/c8923268-e6c6-4233-8a0e-9a5b5d0c3c25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Congress, representation is often used as a fig leave to cover ideological complicity. But while diversity alone does not signal independence, it can matter quite deeply in another dimension.
Institutional representation can certainly influence culture. Will tomorrow's Muslim children envision a broader range of possibilities for their futures because of El-Syed's victory? They very well might, just as Native Americans can see progress and take inspiration from Flanagan's election in Minnesota.
But many Americans of color [felt like the same way](https://substack.com/redirect/35d148f5-b9bb-40a9-9906-ab580de935bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) when Obama was elected. And that feeling--vibes--allowed him to swing to the right as a president and critically [expand](https://substack.com/redirect/37061c57-d406-4271-bed3-ab663a5a32c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the powers of the executive branch. I & many others publicly warned that [executive power was the central issue](https://substack.com/redirect/ee221411-1000-477b-bba4-947e83c35530?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) confronting the Republic, but an illiterate political culture can't recognize patterns in history.
Ultimately, racial & ethnic representation matter far less to policy than people tend to think. There are always opportunists willing to sell out their communities for the sake of their careers. The Congressional Black Caucus, for instance, is among Washington's most reliable sources of support for Wall Street. Its members often take positions that undermine the interests of their constituents, like when Clyburn [kneecapped](https://substack.com/redirect/1ba32549-51f0-402a-9468-ff5c5deac6bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Bernie Sanders in 2016 and ultimately helped [put Trump in office](https://substack.com/redirect/45f719c4-d828-41a0-90e8-796c1037ad36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2020.
Senator-Elect Abdul Syed is not just a Muslim. He's also an epidemiologist and public health administrator. He ran for Congress not to champion the U.S. foreign policy interests of Muslim countries, but rather to help Americans get to a doctor without being driven into bankruptcy.
That kind of _experiential_ representation matters more than his faith, ethnicity, or national origin. It--his background and expertise--could do a lot to inform his seemingly ignorant colleagues in the Senate.
I hope that Senator El Syed is able to crack the discursive dam and help force along overdue public discussion that he already helped advance as a candidate. One hopes that his resounding victory, and the [desperate but revealing response](https://substack.com/redirect/3acd2515-0c96-4ebd-bf60-9b04689aa023?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of other voices in the establishment, help incline other senators to see the writing on the political wall.
### **More to come**
This week's election offers many further observations, including the continuing influence of AIPAC in the next Congress despite the organization's increasingly poisonous support for presidents. I also look forward to observing who in Congress might be best suited for leadership roles given the failures of Democrats under the previous direction of Jeffries & Schumer.
I'm on the road this week, however, for a non-profit Board meeting for [Defending Rights and Dissent](https://substack.com/redirect/b01d7995-7328-4770-96d4-ee6506281ae8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a small and important organization that I encourage readers to explore & support. I'll write again soon to unpack those further themes.
Please feel free to pose questions in the comments in the meantime!

In case you thought Donald Trump and the Republicans were going to learn something from Tuesday's election, I've got news for you: they aren't. Not even a little bit. They are going to double down on all the same stupid, destructive, corrupt, depraved shit they've been doing for the last two years.
We got the clearest sign of that yet when Trump kicked Susie Wiles to the curb and made Stephen Miller his new chief of staff. That is not the move of a man who heard the voters. That is the move of a man who heard them loud and clear and decided to give them the middle finger. Trump isn't course correcting. He isn't going to work with Democrats to get anything done. He's digging in.
And it's a stark reminder that even though we just had an incredible night on Tuesday, one we should be damn proud of, this fight is far from over.
Let's be clear about who Stephen Miller is. He is one of the most disgustingly racist, vile human beings in Donald Trump's orbit. He is the architect of Trump's immigration agenda. He is as corrupt as the rest of them. He regularly goes on television and calls people like me domestic terrorists. He is the embodiment of the evil at the core of this administration.
And now he's running the whole show.
So we have to double and triple down on our work, too.
I know a lot of people want to spend this week on Democratic infighting. This type of candidate did great here. That type of candidate did great there. I get it. Everybody wants to make their point. Put it aside. They are going to do another version of what they did in Minneapolis and Chicago, terrorizing immigrant communities. They're going to steal billions and billions more dollars. They're going to try to hurt people. There will be more war, more violence, more depravity. And we cannot sit back and let it happen.
The Republican Party has used every minute of its time in power to do the most horrendous things it can think of. They've done nothing to help the American people. Meanwhile, the media is wringing its hands about how Democrats need to be careful not to overreach. Ooh, don't lean too hard into the investigations. Ooh, be careful.

Then go back to the American people and ask for more power, because we can show them exactly how government can materially improve their lives. It doesn't have to be a machine that only serves rich and powerful assholes like Elon Musk. We can build something better.

Let's take this for the opportunity it is. Let's prove government can be a force for good. Let's keep building a community of people who love each other and who stand with the most vulnerable people in this country, the ones under attack right now.
And let's do the fucking work, together.
Let's get to work.
With urgency,
--Mike

body:
I am going back on the road, and I would love for you to join me LIVE on Sunday, November 8 at 6:00 PM EST as our new website opens.
---
I am going back on the road, and I would love for you to join me LIVE on Sunday, November 8 at 6:00 PM EST as our new website opens.
| Grassroots Army Garrett is going back into the arena.
---
[](https://9l762.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsDg0fV3Ji0XTonBupr9Lp/9rMPAUIhXjaq)
[GrassrootsArmy.org](https://9l762.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsE8LNhTi46Se4r1Iept3t/ie5tRLLEvIZD)
Friends, I am going back on the road, because the people of this state deserve someone who will meet them where they live. I plan to spend my time in firehouses, town halls, living rooms, and main streets, listening to ordinary people and helping them stand up for the communities they love. Elections come and go, but the work of building strong communities cannot stop when the campaign signs come down. Lasting change happens when everyday citizens stay involved all year long, show up at their school board and township meetings, and keep encouraging their neighbors to take part. | Mark your calendar Join me LIVE on Sunday, November 8 at 6:00 PM EST as the new Grassroots Army website opens. [GrassrootsArmy.org](https://9l762.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsEag5tu6QCNoKuqgToclx/9IcSsAdD0x5P)
---
That is why I would love for you to join me this Sunday, November 8 at 6:00 PM EST, when I will go LIVE to open the new Grassroots Army website and walk you through everything it offers. You can watch a short video about why we are heading back out by clicking either photo in this email.
[](https://9l762.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsF30o6KUmIIyayg4InMU1/QTPg_lvUPdCz)
[Click here to watch the video on YouTube.](https://9l762.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsFVLWIkt8OE8r2VS7m6C5/hEa4fhShVB02)
The website will be our home base, a place we own where we can come together, stay informed, and find practical ways to get involved close to home. Members can enlist and receive a numbered membership card that is theirs for life, and every purchase of Grassroots Army gear helps support the work we are doing together.
Please mark your calendar for Sunday at 6:00 PM EST, and consider forwarding this email to a friend who cares about their community as much as you do. I am grateful for your support, and I look forward to seeing you there.
[GrassrootsArmy.org](https://9l762.r.ag.d.sendibm3.com/mk/cl/f/sh/1t6Af4OiGsFxgEVBHUU9J76Kpwkpu9/D2PrjtKaMrgc)
---
For God and Country,
**Dr. Garrett Soldano D.C.**
Grassroots Army
**GJS Investments LLC**
8357 Barony Pt, Mattawan, MI 49071

**The applause**
There is a moment in "Yorktown," mid-second act of the smash success 'Hamilton', when Daveed Diggs and Okieriete Onaodowan sing the most applauded line in modern musical theater: "Immigrants -- we get the job done." Night after night, the house detonates. Since it opened on Broadway in August 2015, *Hamilton* has won eleven Tony Awards, a Grammy, and the Pulitzer Prize; it became the highest-grossing show in Broadway history and streamed into tens of millions of homes on Disney+ in July 2020. In November 2016 the cast famously stopped a performance to read a statement to Vice-President-elect Pence from the stage, casting the show as a shrine to "the diverse America" anxious about what was coming. Its hero -- "the ten-dollar founding father," the orphan of Nevis and St. Croix who "got a lot farther by working a lot harder" -- is now invoked, without embarrassment, as the patron saint of immigration.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/60953ff2-f260-41ec-90d8-d93f2b36c7f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**The 92 pages**
There is another Hamilton, and it was typeset at the height of America's last great immigration panic. In 1928, Charles Scribner's Sons published a slim, palm-sized volume -- 92 pages -- titled 'The Founders of the Republic on Immigration, Naturalization and Aliens', "collected for and edited by Madison Grant and Chas. Stewart Davison," research work by Oseen Kiley. Grant's name now requires a warning label: the author of 'The Passing of the Great Race', the eugenicist whose pseudo-science helped feed the restrictionist fever that became the Johnson-Reed Act of 1924. Note him, file him away -- and then read the book he compiled, because the editors did something useful: they got out of the way and let the founders testify in their own words. Washington's pages include his 1794 warning to John Adams that immigrants settled "in a body" retain "the language, habits, and principles (good or bad) which they bring with them." And the whole volume hangs on an epigraph from Gouverneur Morris, the pen behind "We the People":...

| | | | Wow, Peter, what a night!
---
Over this past year, I traveled across Virginia and around the country to campaign for Democrats. This week, voters showed up and Democrats won big, from the top of the ticket to the bottom.
Thanks to you, **Shannon Taylor and Elaine Luria** flipped critical seats that helped take back the House, and Virginia is sending our senior senator and incumbent Democratic representatives back to Capitol Hill.
Virginians also made history on the ballot, with our three constitutional amendments passing by overwhelming margins.
We enshrined **reproductive rights** into our Constitution, so no politician can threaten your right to choose, your right to privacy, or your right to contraception.
We enshrined **marriage equality** in our Constitution, affirming that Virginia is a welcoming place for ALL families.
We also guaranteed a **constitutional right to vote** for every eligible Virginian.
These wins reach well beyond our Commonwealth. Across the country, voters flipped Governorships and Senate seats, and sent a clear message that they want leaders who will lower costs, protect their rights, and put people ahead of politics.
_But our work is not done._
Next year, Virginia has critical state House and state Senate races on the ballot. The General Assembly is where we turn what Virginians voted for into real laws that lower costs, protect healthcare, and keep our rights secure.
[**_We can't take any of it for granted. name: Voto Latino
subject: Latinos continue to shape elections.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
Our work doesn’t end here.
#
[](https://act.votolatino.org/go/305?c0=em-ms-voto-20261107-1.zzcpAi&refcode=em20261107-764&t=1&akid=764%2E1366028%2ENeSdch)
Peter,
On Tuesday night, Latino voters reshaped the electoral map once again.
In Texas, California, and other states, Latinos turned out in huge numbers and helped decide control of both the House and the Senate, just two years after many of them backed Republicans in 2024.
In 2024, Republicans won roughly 44% of the Latino vote. This week, that share dropped back to 30%.
In one of our target districts, Texas’s 15th District, which is 82% Hispanic, the margin swung 42 points from 2024. Republicans were so confident they had locked in Latino voters that they redrew five Texas districts around that assumption. On Tuesday, Democrats won four of them.
If this Tuesday showed us anything, it’s that **Latinos don’t just participate in elections._We shape them._** And when someone takes our community for granted, we make sure they hear about it at the ballot box.
But our work doesn’t stop here. In 2027 and 2028, both parties will be fighting for Latino voters like never before, and we need to be ready by registering the millions of young Latinos who turn 18 next year, reaching new voters across the country, and making sure our community is actively participating.

---
My name is Eduardo Verástegui. I produced the film Sound of Freedom, and through **Sound of Freedom Foundation,** I work alongside partners who rescue children from trafficking and give them a real home. **Sound of Freedom Foundation's** partner, House Parent Project, cares for 130 to 150 children every single day. Right now, they have no functioning sewage system for the home they run. Food alone costs House Parent Project over $20,000 a month because of inflation. Building the larger school they need will cost an estimated $60,000, and the reliable vehicles their team needs will cost around $30,000. **Today, a generous donor is matching every gift, dollar for dollar, up to $50,000, to help meet these needs.**
---
[ **Double My Gift Now** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Here’s exactly what your gift helps provide: ✅ A biofilter to replace a septic tank that can’t keep up. ✅ Food, at over $20,000 a month, and that’s before staff, medical care, education, or clothing. ✅ A larger school, an estimated $60,000 to build. ✅ Reliable vehicles, an estimated $30,000, for rescue work and daily needs.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
We’ve only raised $5,000 of the $50,000 match so far. We urgently need your help to cover House Parent Project’s most pressing needs. Today, this match means: **$25 becomes $50**
**$50 becomes $100**
**$100 becomes $200** Your gift helps House Parent Project provide food, care, medical attention, education, clothing, and a safe, functioning place for children to grow.
---
[ **Double My Gift Now** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
For over two decades, House Parent Project has given trafficking survivors a safe home. **Some of those children are now doctors, pastors, missionaries, teachers, and nurses.** They had the chance to build those lives because someone provided what they needed along the way. House Parent Project needs that commitment now. **[Friend, will you give $25, $50, $75, $100, or whatever you can right now to help House Parent Project while your gift is doubled?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
---
[ **Double My Gift Now** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Please give now while this donor’s $50,000 match is still available, so every gift does twice the good. With gratitude and prayer,
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Eduardo Verástegui
Sound of Freedom, Producer
For Sound of Freedom Foundation

For years, billionaires and corporations have played a rigged game — using
their endless wealth to capture the Supreme Court and rewrite the rules of
our economy in their favor.

And working people have paid the price.

With a 6-3 conservative supermajority, the Supreme Court today operates
without accountability, transparency, or independence. Its six right-wing
justices answer to oligarchs, Trump, and extremists — not the American
people.

We can’t fix our economy without fixing the Court. As long as the least
democratic institution in our country has unchecked power, it will keep
rubber-stamping a corporate agenda that puts workers, consumers, and our
democracy at risk.

So how do we take back our economy and courts? By expanding the Supreme
Court.

Adding justices is how we turn a six-person majority into a six-person
minority. It’s how we break their stranglehold for good and restore
balance to the highest court in the country.

Congress has the power to expand the Court. Our job is to build the
pressure that forces lawmakers to use it.

Demand Justice PAC is calling for an expanded bench to unrig our economy,
curb corporate power, and protect working people from this rogue
conservative majority. But it won’t happen on its own. We need your help to organize supporters
and keep Congress feeling the heat until it acts.

Friend, Charlie didn't write an ordinary political book.

Right Wing Revolution is the battle plan he wrote for every American who refuses to sit on the sidelines while the Left tries to tear this country apart. It's a roadmap for winning back our culture... our campuses... and the hearts and minds of young Americans.

**Inside the book, Charlie lays out a vision for an America where:** ✅ Faith and patriotism are celebrated, not silenced

✅ Our borders are secure and our Constitution is respected

✅ We trust our neighbors and feel safe in our communities

✅ The next generation grows up loving this country That vision is alive every time Turning Point USA steps onto a campus. It's alive in every student who hears the truth for the first time and realizes they're not alone.

Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

| | | |

Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

While so many underestimated Gina, I never doubted what she was capable of.
I saw it in the excitement of Texans who showed up to hear her speak, energized by her vision for our state and ready for a change after years of Greg Abbott's failed leadership.
I saw it in the polls, as she surged ahead of Abbott in the final weeks of the campaign, defying expectations and proving that Texas was ready for something different.
**But most of all, I saw it in Gina herself.** In her determination to fight for the people of Texas, her courage to take on the odds, and her unwavering belief that our state deserved better.
**And on Tuesday night, Gina turned that belief into a historic victory.**
But Gina wasn’t the only Democratic pro-choice woman who won big in Texas.
**Vikki Goodwin was elected lieutenant governor** , giving Gina a fellow EMILYs List woman as a partner in statewide leadership. **Four EMILYs List women defeated Republican incumbents on the Texas Supreme Court**. In TX-23, **Katy Padilla Stout** defeated her far-right Republican opponent. And we reelected pro-choice champions like **Lizzie Fletcher** and **Sylvia Garcia** to Congress.
These were all hard-fought victories in a state that so many had written off. But we knew better.
As an EMILYs List board member, I couldn’t be prouder of what this community accomplished. And as a Texan, I couldn’t be more excited about what comes next.

clean_body: I couldn't be prouder of my friend Gina Hinojosa | = We did it, y’all. It’s Wendy Davis — former Texas state senator, proud EMILYs List board member, and lifelong fighter for a better Texas. After decades of hard work, organizing, and investing in Democratic women, Texas has elected our first Democratic governor in more than 30 years. And that governor is my dear friend, EMILYs List-endorsed Gina Hinojosa! I’ve spent years fighting for change in Texas, including taking on Greg Abbott myself. I know firsthand how difficult these races can be. And I know just how extraordinary Gina's victory is. = | = While so many underestimated Gina, I never doubted what she was capable of. I saw it in the excitement of Texans who showed up to hear her speak, energized by her vision for our state and ready for a change after years of Greg Abbott's failed leadership. I saw it in the polls, as she surged ahead of Abbott in the final weeks of the campaign, defying expectations and proving that Texas was ready for something different. But most of all, I saw it in Gina herself. In her determination to fight for the people of Texas, her courage to take on the odds, and her unwavering belief that our state deserved better. And on Tuesday night, Gina turned that belief into a historic victory. But Gina wasn’t the only Democratic pro-choice woman who won big in Texas. Vikki Goodwin was elected lieutenant governor , giving Gina a fellow EMILYs List woman as a partner in statewide leadership. Four EMILYs List women defeated Republican incumbents on the Texas Supreme Court. In TX-23, Katy Padilla Stout defeated her far-right Republican opponent. And we reelected pro-choice champions like Lizzie Fletcher and Sylvia Garcia to Congress. These were all hard-fought victories in a state that so many had written off. But we knew better. As an EMILYs List board member, I couldn’t be prouder of what this community accomplished. Friend,

Stand In The Gap Foundation was born out of January 6. For years, we stood beside those families. We paid for lawyers, covered rent, sat in courtrooms, and made sure nobody went through it alone.

What we learned in those years is why I'm writing to you today.

**The lawfare that came down on January 6 families wasn't built for them, and it didn't stop with them.**

So we widened the fight. Everything we built for those families now lives inside our Stand for Justice initiative, and Stand for Justice is now open to anyone the federal system has run over.

January 6 families aren't going anywhere. They're still with us. They're just no longer the only ones we can help.

Yesterday, I mailed the letter that opens this new chapter.

It went to the Office of the Pardon Attorney at the U.S. Department of Justice. It's about a man named Dr. Michael Rimlawi. His patients call him Dr. Mike.

Dr. Mike is a spine surgeon from Dallas. For twenty years, people came to him when they couldn't sit through a workday, couldn't pick up their kids, couldn't sleep through the night. He did the small-incision kind of spine surgery. Less cutting, less blood, and most patients home the same day or the next.

Then the federal government went after the hospital where he operated.

Forest Park Medical Center paid a marketing firm to advertise its surgeons, something hospitals all over this country do every day. Prosecutors called it a kickback. Dr. Mike wasn't charged with hurting a patient. He wasn't charged with billing for a surgery that never happened.

A jury convicted him in 2019. In 2021, a federal judge sentenced him to 90 months in prison, seven and a half years, and ordered him to pay $28,839,201.68 in restitution.

To insurance companies.

The Supreme Court refused to hear his case. Justice Gorsuch wrote that he would have heard it, because a judge, not a jury, set that $28.8 million.

Dr. Mike did his time. He's home now with his wife and their two young sons. But unless something changes, that debt follows him for twenty years after his release. And a pardon alone won't erase it. The pardon has to say so.

So our letter asks for two things: a full pardon, and that the pardon wipe out every dollar of restitution he hasn't paid.

Friend, Dr. Mike was nowhere near the Capitol. But if you've followed what happened to January 6 families, you already know this story. A prosecution built to make an example. A sentence that ends on paper and keeps going in real life. Restitution that follows a man home and sits at his kitchen table.

Different courtroom. Same pattern.

That's why Dr. Mike is the first story we're telling from the new Stand for Justice. He won't be the last.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/29eb07cb-924f-49d6-b403-c5242640b3ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Idaho Dems put out a chart this week bragging that they "made gains across the map in 2026."
They said they're "building momentum, expanding our reach, and we're not backing down."
Well, in some places, yes.
But not across the board like they claim in this chart:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ccb95d68-db8e-4412-ac03-a66949b834f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It looks daunting, but it's not an apples-to-apples comparison.
Because Idaho voters still showed up big time and murdered Prop 1 (with the Yes side raising about $1M more than us). They also said YES to the English language constitutional amendment I sponsored, and Republicans held every statewide seat.
Bottom line: Idaho is still VERY MUCH Republican territory (one of the few).
Here's the proof from my district in Nampa ([numbers taken from Ballotpedia](https://substack.com/redirect/1ca87099-4df1-4703-8ba9-79c494cfcf95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)).
**First, let 's look at my seat:**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f3e7c81d-e473-49f3-9261-1cf0e643637c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Democrat got 105 FEWER votes than last time:
* 2024: 6,427
* 2026: 6,322

With millions poured into Prop 1 to drive turnout, they still lost votes in Nampa.
And my votes this midterm compared to last midterm?
* 2022: 10,091
* 2026: 10,088

(Roughly the same.)
But in 2022 the Dems got ZERO votes because they couldn't be bothered to even put a name on the ballot.
You see what they did there? The Dems' "30.0% to 38.5%" compares a Trump year to a midterm. Presidential-year voters stayed home on both sides. But mine showed up like they always do, and theirs shrank.
Now my seatmate, Rep. Brent Crane ([Ballotpedia](https://substack.com/redirect/216cc1fb-7236-41cc-8533-a8a894468d80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)).
Here's his chart:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7d8c13ca-7de9-40c4-91c1-9ac73a9db08b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* 2022 Dem: ZERO (they didn't run anybody)
* 2024 Dem: 6,073
* 2026 Dem: 6,188

Brent faced the same Democrat in 2024 and 2026. But the Dem only got 115 more votes, even with Prop 1 on the ballot to drive their turnout.
Brent's midterms:
* 2022: 9,476
* 2026: 10,209

So Brent picked up +733 votes from 2022 to 2026.
Now my other seatmate, Rep. Steve Tanner ([Ballotpedia](https://substack.com/redirect/a27b870a-3004-439a-b9e9-65faeb234f40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)).
Here's his chart:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a2620947-d351-4667-9228-1acaba3e5b38?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Funny how his seat isn't on the Dems' list.
* 2022 Dem: ZERO (they didn't run anybody)
* 2024 Dem: ZERO (they didn't run anybody)
* 2026 Dem: 6,091

That's the lowest Democrat total of the three District 13 races this year, with Prop 1 on the ballot to drive their turnout.
Now the GOP vote for his seat, midterm to midterm:
* 2022: 10,113
* 2026: 10,254

So again, there was no surge. Republicans picked up +141 votes for Steve's seat from 2022 to 2026.
That's how District 13 is doing. All three Republican seats held their midterm vote or grew it. And in 2022, Dems didn't put a name on the ballot for any of them.
So next time somebody shares that graphic in your feed, drop one of these charts under it.

Team, **We’ve flipped Minnesota’s First Congressional District from red to blue.** I’m still taking it in. This victory belongs to you. It belongs to the neighbors who knocked doors, chipped in what they could, hosted a living room conversation, put up a yard sign, or told a friend why this race mattered. Two years ago, some would’ve said we stood no chance – _but you gave us this chance._ I’ll have more to say in the coming days. But unfortunately it’s not quite over yet: With the margin where it is, we might be going to a recount. Here’s why. Peter – While much of the country’s attention was focused on Election Day this week, our work to protect families continued here in Washington. And this week, our office secured a major victory. A King County Superior Court judge ordered Albertsons to pay **$900 million for its role in fueling Washington’s opioid crisis** , plus fees and costs. This is believed to be the largest verdict in state history. This victory concludes a multi-year case in which our office proved that Albertsons repeatedly failed to investigate and resolve warning signs that opioid prescriptions could be misused or diverted into the illicit drug market. Between 2006 and 2022, Albertsons pharmacies dispensed more than 641 million opioid pills into Washington. **Our office showed that the company unlawfully filled prescriptions with warning signs more than 6.5 million times without adequately documenting that they were written for legitimate medical purposes.** **The evidence also showed that Albertsons prioritized profits over patient and customer safety** , discouraging pharmacists from identifying problematic prescriptions and failing to provide the staffing and oversight needed to prevent dangerous drugs from reaching our communities. The consequences of these failures have been devastating. **More than 26,000 Washingtonians have died from opioid overdoses since 1999, including more than 7,400 in just the last three years.** This verdict cannot undo the devastating harms of the opioid crisis. But it will provide desperately needed resources to support treatment and prevent future crises. Since the beginning of the opioid crisis, our office has recovered $2.17 billion for state and local governments. This latest victory will expand those efforts and help communities across Washington continue addressing the damage caused by this epidemic. **[If you believe in holding powerful corporations accountable and standing up for Washington communities, I hope you’ll consider making a contribution today.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143085340/659033527/-2020589092?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&refcode=AU_NWB_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20261107_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDY5NjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjE2NjFmZmQtZTRkYS1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=2tyleAm_1lgWKjfYMnMf-qqhfyvEy0FyudhOR7R0Mfo=)** | | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143085342/659033529/-2020589092?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&refcode=AU_NWB_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20261107_PM1_V1_S2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDY5NjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjE2NjFmZmQtZTRkYS1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=2tyleAm_1lgWKjfYMnMf-qqhfyvEy0FyudhOR7R0Mfo=)

We have all put in a LOT of hard work over the course of this campaign. But hard work is good work – and the work isn’t quite done. At this point, we are still down 233 votes, but that number will change very soon. The State Board of Elections is reporting that thousands of ballots across our district are still being tallied. I trust the election process and know that the local boards of elections across Eastern North Carolina are doing the work to ensure all mail-in and provisional ballots are counted. At the end of the day, every voice will be heard. And when they are, I believe that we will come out victorious in this election. ** I am so proud of what we’ve accomplished on this campaign. We listened to voters' concerns about our country regardless of what side of the aisle they fall on. We shared our positive vision for the future. And when we win, I’m going to go to Washington to represent ALL people in this district – Democrat, Republican, Independent, or completely tuned out altogether. This is a responsibility I don’t take lightly. We have a lot of hard work ahead of us. * * *
In late August, when the darling of the DSA, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said "Woke 1.0 was crazy," everyone quickly realized that the existence of "Woke 1.0" implied there would be a 'Woke 2.0."
After the blue tsunami reshaped the American political landscape last Tuesday, the implications of what "Woke 2.0" might entail are fresh on everyone's minds. Are we set to go back to the era of pulling down statues, inventing new genders, and being forced to put pronouns in your bio?
One of the few rays of hope emerging from the 2026 midterm elections come from state ballot measures. While voters overwhelmingly split for Democrats, a surprising number of conservative-leaning referendums and initiatives were passed.
Several states who flipped blue also enacted voter identification requirements. Although North Carolina flipped their Senate seat over to Democrat Roy Cooper, they passed an amendment that expanded their voter ID requirements. A similar constitutional amendment passed in Ohio, requiring photo ID for in-person and mail-in voting. Nevada also tightened their ID requirements for voting.
Alaska, Arkansas, Kansas, South Dakota, and West Virginia all approved measures specifying that only US citizens were eligible to vote in elections. Even though Kansas flipped their senate seat blue and lost their house supermajority, voters still opted to enshrine citizenship requirements.
Transgenderism was also on the ballots in many states. In Nebraska, Initiative Measure 422 passed, which placed restrictions on transgender participation in school sports. Because 422 was installed as a constitutional amendment, it would be extremely difficult for lawmakers to reverse. In Colorado, Proposition 134 and Proposition 135 placed restrictions on transgender surgeries for minors and separated school sports by gender. In Arizona, Proposition 318 also passed, expanding sex-based restrictions in bathrooms, locker rooms, and even in private schools.
* * *
# **We 're not giving up this fight, and neither should you**
Tuesday was a wake up call to all American patriots...
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d56157ec-c878-4942-a07a-0444df905f36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The battle ahead will surely be hard and up-hill. But think of the brave Americans who stormed the beaches of Normandy, or the men who fought and bled at Shiloh and Lexington.
They had a dream for America they were willing to die for. We cannot let their sacrifice be in vain.
This is what we believe in.
We must fight for our nation with everything we have within us, even on the darkest days, as our ancestors did.
### **PolitiBrawl will hold our place in line on the battleground for information and news.**
We appreciate your readership and support.
Do not give up hope. Tomorrow is a brighter day.
* * *
_**(Piece continues):**_
Arizona had another win on Tuesday, despite landing a Democrat trifecta just two years after they swung red for the 2024 Presidential election. Arizona Proposition 316 prohibited their local governments from increasing the grocery sales tax without voter approval. Further, it capped that tax rate at 2%. Florida also passed a tax exemption amendment, increasing their homestead property tax exemption.
In Idaho, voters rejected Proposition 1, which was an attempt to expand abortion access in the state. Proposition 1 was a citizen initiative rather than a referendum passed by the legislature, showing that Idahoans were passionate about preserving pro-life protections in their state.
Despite these wins, there were of course losses. Arizona, California, and Colorado failed to expand their voter ID requirements, and Nevada voted to allow the right to an abortion. In Los Angeles, their city council approved legal protections for polyamorous couples, giving rights to those engaged in multi-person relationships.
In the age of personality politics, where candidates are required to build up cult-like followings, ballot measures offer us an insight into the broader culture. Separated from individuals, voters leaned into traditional conservative agendas. They rejected radical gender ideology and tax hikes while embracing election security efforts.
Woke 2.0 is a very real and present danger. With socialism on the rise in the US, especially among young people, Democrat politicians will be eager to run as far to the left as possible to maintain their liberal purity. If the more traditional Democrats want to keep themselves from being eaten alive, they will have to keep pace with AOC, Zohran Mamdani, and Bernie Sanders.
However, Tuesday's ballot measures and 2024's populism craze both tell us that our culture still sees "woke" as cringey. When radical Democrats are left in the driver's seat, they will return to the policies that have made them historically unpalatable. They will return to their worst instincts, propping up the identity politics that make them so unpopular with voters. If Woke 1.0 was crazy, Woke 2.0 might be worse. But at least whatever wild, wacky, and unhinged progressivism the left chooses to embrace over the coming years will show Americans that they're too "craaaaazy" to be in control.
* * *

As we described in her lawsuit, Luka was a deeply troubled teenager. Her parents had divorced. She struggled with anxiety, isolation, school, panic attacks, self-harm, and thoughts of suicide. Then she encountered transgender influencers online. At 15, Luka began receiving gender-related care. At 16, doctors removed her breasts. Testosterone came months later. Luka now alleges that the medical professionals who treated her failed to provide the proper standard of care and failed to obtain informed consent. **Her case is headed toward a jury trial currently scheduled for June, 2027.** **But the legal battle is already raging. **Right now, the defendants are challenging expert testimony Luka intends to present regarding the standard of care. **These kinds of fights mean more motions, more legal work, more time, and more expense. **

Now she wants a jury to hear what happened to her. But getting Luka into that courtroom has become a battle of its own. I'm Mark Trammell, CEO of theCenter for American Liberty , a nonprofit public interest law firm that takes on cases many organizations won't touch. And I'm asking you to help us fight for Luka. As we described in her lawsuit, Luka was a deeply troubled teenager. Her parents had divorced. She struggled with anxiety, isolation, school, panic attacks, self-harm, and thoughts of suicide. Then she encountered transgender influencers online. At 15, Luka began receiving gender-related care. At 16, doctors removed her breasts. Testosterone came months later. Luka now alleges that the medical professionals who treated her failed to provide the proper standard of care and failed to obtain informed consent. Her case is headed toward a jury trial currently scheduled for June, 2027. But the legal battle is already raging. Right now, the defendants are challenging expert testimony Luka intends to present regarding the standard of care. These kinds of fights mean more motions, more legal work, more time, and more expense. And that can become a strategy all its own -- make litigation so long and expensive that the other side runs out of resources. We refuse to let that happen. We've been here before. The Center for American Liberty represents detransitioner Chloe Cole in her lawsuit against the medical providers she alleged harmed her. The hospital defendants aggressively filed motions delaying Chloe's trial by years. We fought back and now Chloe's trial is scheduled for April. We are prepared to fight just as hard for Luka. But unlike the powerful institutions we face, the Center for American Liberty is a nonprofit. We depend on Americans like you. This is why our organization exists. There are Americans all across this country who have been silenced, pushed out, or left to fight powerful institutions alone. We stand beside them. And we fight. I came to the Center for American Liberty because I wanted to get my hands dirty and be in the courtroom fighting these cases because somebody has to do it. Derek, Look, when I first jumped into the race to beat Cindy Hyde-Smith, the national pundits didn’t really know what to expect. They wrote us off. My first campaign event had four people. Now, we’re on the verge of making history and flipping Mississippi’s Senate race. And it’s all thanks to one thing: GRASSROOTS DONORS. That’s why, all along the walls of my office, I’ve hung photos of people we’ve met on the campaign trail. They remind me to take a little bit of joy in the campaign. [](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-colom-split.wz-auy&refcode=em_20261107_10251_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=10251%2E22930333%2EkNPIO3) **These photos remind me of why I’m in this race. The people of Mississippi are finally getting the attention they deserve and I am proud to be fighting for the people of Mississippi in this moment.** But our work is far from over. We need to make sure that we are able to protect the will of the voters. _If we want to do it right - and we HAVE to do it right - it’s going to cost millions and millions of dollars._ I will always stand up and fight for Mississippi. Now, I’m asking you to stand with me. Friend, my name is Eduardo Verastegui. I produced the film _Sound of Freedom_.

That film moved millions of people to ask, "_What can I do_?"

**Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists to answer that question, by helping stop the sale of God's children.

I want to tell you about this girl, because her story shows exactly what it takes to save a child.

**Her name is not Lyra, but this is her true story.**

Lyra grew up in a home where NO ONE kept her safe.

Her mother let the men she brought home hurt her little girl. Then those men brought their friends.

For years, Lyra was abused and trafficked inside her own home.

Through all of it, she never stopped going to school. She was a straight-A student who dreamed of a better life.

At twelve, she found out where her father lived. She ran to him, believing everything would finally change.

**It only got worse**.

Her father began abusing her too. _Then he handed her over to other men. _

[](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=0ac600b72f5f4bb1b4f05d46e62339cd&_e=MktuM-AnXYl5rKgeQp5NPxi-wo3Enm65qaP8_BZhCqEc7eXaCsZvACIMo6W7OJXHCv6dG27JIvPh2q1DEQxw3VpcuatsugDIWLNZHUpEdMRRRee3yDVUBh78dHKtK5Ym74Z3FTmxEhOx_06Q7CqGIELlBWFwlWFcAgNVuxoIwbg1yJPkoyPtbM-vjqU-iUrEff6RnWKN2c4S_ERGW-u2hepta7ILPF3u_IdaWdnW2AaYxh26XpO-y77XwjtF09nccB38uY6njQMn9wam0OQx4tkkwS-ZkR-IxLkk6ngovxzVGxNrV_2BIFvxTwWRzH9R9UX7gjgE__qWl5KctDpGYbpe8M3KMOenY4fDFY1cxISrxiL8WpOUC-3DoLXmh5CmzMWJf7Bx7yMAOELL4F8Abh_nobo_3UVjsE8R_V1Wdm7gdnn4OJNdMdF65R4ndZrgFZkJpqttGgEeGOIqFUjT3y1tZst5C4SniQTQhHnL2z3h-iiEirCcY-29fKcWIJYv854BoRaOB-D4AkLOzJp4mNpzV-ZRbrl6J4XFDECx-YWnLLba7NkRNZ4byh-kBp-BgIXOE0sFxuVwisXeVspYA6Q_MzUt_CxSaPAQqo-AeB-cuk2Toi0bLUtxrkihYY_t7I7EqnkwfPd6--64b8iu8Dcw9-nLwWpZ0N7vi4DnNBk%3D)

A couple of years later, that hospital called one of the rescue partners we support.

Police officers escorted our partner to a small private room in the back, where Lyra was waiting.

"I sat beside her," our partner told me, "and slowly, she began to trust me."

Then the tears came, and the whole story came out.

We need to make sure that we stand up for the will of the voters from now until this is fully certified. In a state like Mississippi, we can’t afford to get complacent at the finish line. Closing this race out is going to cost millions of dollars. This is going to be one of the most closely divided U.S. Senate races in modern American history. [So please. clean_body: | | | | | Hey, Peter, it’s Scott. I was born and raised in Mississippi. Growing up here, I never thought I would be locked in what is shaping up to be one of the closest Senate races in modern history. Getting here wasn’t easy. But over the last fourteen months my campaign has traveled all across the state, speaking with every last voter we could find. We even spent some time talking to voters outside Trump’s Mississippi rally last month – because that’s how you win in a state like this. Along the way we’ve been funded by grassroots donations of $5, $10, even $50 at a time. And it means the world to me to know that so many people have my back. But this race isn’t over yet. We need to make sure that we stand up for the will of the voters from now until this is fully certified. In a state like Mississippi, we can’t afford to get complacent at the finish line. Closing this race out is going to cost millions of dollars. name: Steven Andersen
subject: More Ways to Fight Government Corruption

Dear Fellow Patriot, As 2026 draws to a close, I want to express my sincere gratitude for your generous support of Judicial Watch. Your commitment makes our important work possible, and we are deeply grateful to have you standing with us in the fight against government corruption. As you review your year-end charitable giving plans, I hope you'll consider the many ways you can continue to support our mission. From a special year-end gift to tax-advantaged giving options and planned gifts, there are several ways to make a difference for Judicial Watch that help us pursue accountability, defend the rule of law, and hold government officials accountable.
1. **Become a Monthly Amicus Donor and Fight Corruption Every Month**

Provide dependable support for Judicial Watch's work throughout the year by becoming a monthly Amicus donor. Your recurring contribution helps us plan ahead and pursue important investigations and lawsuits. To get started, visit our secure donation page: _[jwatch.us/amicus](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86463&L=32388&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL2pvaW4tdGhlLWFtaWN1cy1zb2NpZXR5Lz91dG1fc291cmNlPWRlcGxveWVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3JzJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUNNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRA==&H=aeae6aaa203f487a07b69d536dec297c4fa3a99a4e12ffff74f6723d1719869d)_
2. **Make a Special Year-End Gift**

A year-end contribution helps Judicial Watch continue its fight for government transparency, accountability, and the rule of law. If you're considering an additional charitable gift before the end of the year, we hope you'll make Judicial Watch part of your plans. Make your gift securely online: [www.JudicialWatch.org/donate](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86463&L=2347&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL21ha2UtYS1jb250cmlidXRpb24tMi8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&H=2550f7d2eca75528cc68c8eefa1a951114f669e91af9a49dcc68d9ffdb2eed8a)
3. **Give Directly from Your IRA Through a Qualified Charitable Distribution (QCD)**

If you are age 701⁄2 or older, you may be eligible to make a Qualified Charitable Distribution directly from your IRA to Judicial Watch. A QCD can offer significant tax advantages while supporting our work. Eligible QCDs can count toward your Required Minimum Distribution (RMD) and are generally excluded from federal taxable income, subject to applicable tax rules. You do not need to itemize deductions to benefit from this giving strategy. **Important:** To qualify, the distribution must be made directly by your IRA custodian to Judicial Watch. Do not withdraw the funds yourself and then donate them. You may also be able to use a QCD to fund a Charitable Gift Annuity with Judicial Watch, subject to eligibility requirements. Call **(888) 593-8442** to learn more.
4. **Donate Appreciated Stocks or Mutual Funds**

Donating appreciated stocks or mutual funds you have held for more than one year may provide a valuable tax advantage. You may be able to deduct the fair market value of the donated assets, subject to applicable limitations, while avoiding capital gains tax on the appreciation. Instead of selling appreciated investments and donating the proceeds, consider donating the assets directly to Judicial Watch. Call **(888) 593-8442** to learn how to make a gift of appreciated securities.
5. **Establish a Charitable Gift Annuity and Receive Income for Life**

If you are age 55 or older, you may be able to establish a Charitable Gift Annuity (CGA) with Judicial Watch with a gift of $5,000 or more. A CGA can provide fixed payments for life while supporting Judicial Watch's mission. Depending on your circumstances, it may also offer potential tax benefits. To learn more about this unique giving opportunity, call **(888) 593-8442**.
6. **Recommend a Grant from Your Donor-Advised Fund**

If you have a Donor-Advised Fund (DAF), consider recommending a grant to Judicial Watch. Your fund provides a convenient way to direct charitable resources toward the fight for government accountability. Contact your DAF sponsor to recommend a grant to Judicial Watch.
7. **Include Judicial Watch in Your Will or Estate Plans**

A planned gift can help protect the principles you care about for generations to come. By including Judicial Watch in your will or other estate plans, you can leave a lasting legacy in support of government transparency, accountability, and freedom. We would be happy to provide information about the different ways to include Judicial Watch in your plans, including our brochure, _How to Make a Will That Works_. To learn more, call **(888) 593-8442** or reply to this email. Thank you again for your generous support of Judicial Watch. We are grateful for your partnership and for your commitment to our mission. Whatever way you choose to give, your generosity helps us continue the fight against government corruption and work toward a government that is accountable to the American people. Sincerely, Steven C. Andersen
Director of Development
Judicial Watch 425 Third Street S.W.
Suite 800
Washington, D.C. 20024 [www.judicialwatch.org](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=86463&L=39135&F=H&drurl=aHR0cDovL3d3dy5KdWRpY2lhbFdhdGNoLm9yZy8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1NYXkmdXRtX3Rlcm09Tm9uLURvbm9ycyZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1DTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0Q=&H=415618f9342493823f42b3c56372c33e6731a06a14e82ec965c373094fa6f20e) P.S. There are many ways to support Judicial Watch beyond a traditional cash donation. Whether through appreciated stock, an IRA charitable distribution, or a planned gift, we'd be happy to help you explore the option that's right for you. Call us at (888) 593-8442 or simply reply to this email._

_ | Judicial Watch, Inc.
425 Third Street SW, Suite 800
Washington, DC 20024

name: Nicole Kelly
subject: Are you upset about 2026?
body:
Non-citizens on the rolls, ballots counted days late, machines that won’t work. We can fix this.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e17539757/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvTkY4VFN3akczWQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDc/LbmNseWdCU1I3WQ/qP2hpZHM9bmMwWnJTMzhhc0JYNnhscw/gau-yiw/sdn2b8069db)
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-yiw/s8odadc2962)
---
| | | Patriot,
---
I’ll be honest with you. I’m frustrated with how the 2026 midterms turned out, and if you’re reading this, I’d guess you are too. Look at what we watched happen this cycle. On Election Day, ballot scanners failed across Westchester County, **New York** , in one of the closest House races in the country, held by a Republican incumbent, and poll workers stuffed completed ballots into emergency bags saying they would just be counted later. In **California** , federal officials flagged roughly 20,000 likely non-citizens who had been mailed ballots, and an appeals court let the state count them anyway. **New Jersey** admitted it found 6,600 non-citizens on its own voter rolls. And in one **California** county, election staff opened a locked drop box and found nearly 600 sealed ballots that had sat there uncounted for five months after the election was certified. On top of all that, the Supreme Court ruled this summer that 14 states and D.C. can keep counting mail ballots that arrive after Election Day. **_Election Day is supposed to mean one day._** After a night like this, it’s tempting to tune out and wait for things to cool down. I _understand that feeling._ But these problems don’t fix themselves between elections. If we look away now, every one of them will be bigger in 2028, and liberals will do everything they can to steal the presidential election. _**[If you’re upset about how 2026 turned out and you want to make sure 2028 is decided by honest votes, I need your help right now.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-yiw/s8odadc2962)**_
---
[ **SAVE OUR ELECTIONS!** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-yiw/s8odadc2962)
---
I serve on the board of **Save Election Day**. We’re a team of volunteer election lawyers who have worked Election Days, early voting, and recounts, so we’ve seen these problems up close. We’re a 501(c)4 non-profit founded for one purpose: **to carry President Trump’s election reforms into the states and turn them into law.** Here’s why the states matter. Washington, D.C. keeps introducing election bills that stall, and even when Congress acts, elections are still run under state law. So we write the bills, push them through statehouses, and take the fight straight to voters with ballot measures where legislatures won’t move. Our goals are simple:
---
* Photo voter ID for every voter
* One national Election Day, with results on Election Night
* No more ballots counted days after the polls close
* Shorter mail-in and early voting windows
* Only American citizens voting in American elections

---
We’re already at work in states like Nevada and Georgia, and we’re ready to expand. The time to protect 2028 is right now, while legislatures prepare for their next sessions. By the time the presidential race heats up, the rules will already be set. _**[Will you give $25 today to help Save Election Day fix these problems before 2028?](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-yiw/s8odadc2962)**_
---
[ **SAVE OUR ELECTIONS!** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-yiw/s8odadc2962)
---
Your gift goes straight into drafting these laws and getting them passed, state by state.
---
| | | Thank you, Nicole Kelly Co-Founder and President
Save Election Day
---
P.S. Every problem we saw this cycle traces back to a rule written at the state level, and those rules can be rewritten. That work has to start now if we want it in place for 2028. _**[Please give today to support our work.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-yiw/s8odadc2962)**_
